title: Design and Implementation of IoT-enabled Intelligent Irrigation System Using Machine Learning
source_title: Proceedings 2023 28th Asia Pacific Conference on Communications Apcc 2023
title_norm: design and implementation of iotenabled intelligent irrigation system using machine learning
abstract: Water scarcity poses a significant challenge to sustainable cultivation, driven by geographical and environmental factors. Traditional irrigation systems fall short in effectively addressing water shortage. Precision agriculture offers a promising solution by optimizing production and minimizing water usage. This study introduces a smart irrigation system that incorporates essential parameters such as soil moisture, humidity, temperature, and wind speed. Additionally, a decision-making method based on collected sensor data is implemented in a microcontroller. Four classification algorithms are assessed using RStudio to determine the most accurate algorithm for the specific scenario. Experimental testing over a ten-day period reveals an irrigation water consumption of approximately 1 liter, with a relatively low detection speed of around 1 second, which can be attributed to using a small pot for testing purposes.

title: Smart Irrigation System Using Arduino
source_title: 2023 Advances in Science and Engineering Technology International Conferences Aset 2023
title_norm: smart irrigation system using arduino
abstract: Climate change exacerbates the competition on a resource (water) already experiences shortage around the world. Irrigation one of the crucial competitors of water. Optimizing irrigation water use has becomes standing objective for long time. Efficient irrigation systems have been designed to optimize irrigation water use. Efficient irrigation is defined as an application of the exact amount of water at the exact time to the soil around the needy plant. To help apply the exact amount (volume flow rate) of water at the right timing, smart and automatic irrigation system was designed, built, and tested. The smart irrigation system comprises of several components (sensors, automatic valves and pump) automatically communicate through Arduino (controller). The sensors detect the soil moisture and determine the exact amount of water required. Then the sensors communicate with the pump and the valves via the controller to apply the proper amount of water at the time it is required. Based on the pump flow rate, timers are used to stop the pump when the required amount of water is applied. Regardless of the difficulties encountered the smart irrigation system was successfully designed and a prototype was built and tested. The different system's components were, matched, tested for compatibility, and assembled. The software that facilitates the communication between the different system's components was developed, installed, and tested. Then the system's workability and operation ability were tested. At the beginning there were some complications hindered the system to run smoothly. The complications include: mal functioning of the moisture sensors; moisture readings were qualitative (high/low); Arduino failed to receive information from multiple sensors; the dripping nozzles were leaking. After taking care of these problems the system was running smoothly. However, the smart irrigation system was found to be versatile, flexible, and working effectively

source_title: 2021 Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology Asiancon 2021
title_norm: smart irrigation system using iot based control valve
abstract: For over decades, the traditional irrigation methods are ditch irrigation, sprinkler system, and drip irrigation. The traditional irrigation systems have uncontrolled irrigation practices, waterlogging, soil deterioration, wastage of water and require continuous human intervention leading to higher usage of electricity and uneven growth of plants. source_title: 3rd International Conference on Advancements in Smart Secure and Intelligent Computing Assic 2025
title_norm: revolutionizing malaysian agriculture with ubiquitous technologies bridging the gap between tradition and innovation
abstract: In recent years, the agriculture sector of Malaysia has required more advanced technologies to improve farming techniques, as traditional methods are inefficient and timeconsuming. These inefficiencies could potentially slow Malaysia's economic growth and undermine the foundation of agriculture in the future. This research investigates and introduces currently available ubiquitous technologies capable of resolving agricultural challenges while enhancing efficiency, food security, and productivity. The study examines existing problems in Malaysia's agriculture sector and provides actionable suggestions for implementing ubiquitous technologies. It also outlines recommended processes for the Malaysian government and agriculture sector to adopt emergent technologies. Relevant literature reviews and successful case studies are included to support both theoretical and practical approaches to ubiquitous computing implementation. The research further explores how these technologies can improve Malaysia's economic growth.

abstract: In this case Internet of Things (IoT) based smart farming is a revolution sample for modernization of agriculture and made them more sustainable. Instead, through the network of sensors, cameras, and drones, the system continuously acquires data on soil moisture, temperature, light intensity, and the like. Apart from the issue of food insecurity this approach also takes care of the destruction of the environment by practices such as large scale monoculture farming by directing the society to the right course to a sustainable agriculture.

title: Long-Range Low-Power Electronic System for Drip Irrigation in Precision Agriculture
source_title: 2023 IEEE Conference on Agrifood Electronics Cafe 2023 Proceedings
title_norm: longrange lowpower electronic system for drip irrigation in precision agriculture
abstract: Nowadays, food security is threatened by population growth, wars, climate change, and desertification due to human activities. Precision agriculture is a novel concept to minimize the usage of natural resources in the agriculture field, mitigating the anthropological effects. This is possible by adopting electronic systems to measure plants' requirements and to make optimal decisions on the crop, avoiding wastefulness. One critical aspect of agriculture is the handling of potable water: an essential resource for all living entities. This paper proposes a long-range, low-power electronic system for drip irrigation in orchards, especially Actinidia and apple trees, to control the distributed water to the cultivars. In this way, the irrigation cycle depends on the plants' needs, saving water and energy resources. The node communicates using LoRa radiofrequency protocol, and it can be used in rural areas where no internet connection is present.

title: A neuromorphic continuous soil monitoring system for precision irrigation
source_title: 2025 IEEE Conference on Agrifood Electronics Cafe 2025
title_norm: a neuromorphic continuous soil monitoring system for precision irrigation
abstract: Sensory processing at the edge requires ultra-low power stand-alone computing technologies. This is particularly true for modern agriculture and precision irrigation systems which aim to optimize water usage by monitoring key environmental observables continuously using distributed efficient embedded processing elements. Neuromorphic processing systems are emerging as a promising technology for extreme edgecomputing applications that need to run on resource-constrained hardware. As such, they are a very good candidate for implementing efficient water management systems based on data measured from soil and plants, across large fields. In this work, we present a fully energy-efficient neuromorphic irrigation control system that operates autonomously without any need for data transmission or remote processing. Leveraging the properties of a biologically realistic spiking neural network, our system performs computation, and decision-making locally. We validate this approach using real-world soil moisture data from apple and kiwi orchards applied to a mixed-signal neuromorphic processor, and show that the generated irrigation commands closely match those derived from conventional methods across different soil depths. Our results show that local neuromorphic inference can maintain decision accuracy, paving the way for autonomous, sustainable irrigation solutions at scale.

title: WSN in coffee cultivation
source_title: Proceeding IEEE International Conference on Computing Communication and Automation Iccca 2016
title_norm: wsn in coffee cultivation
abstract: India ranks sixth in the world in terms of production of coffee. As India being predominantly a tea consuming nation, about 80% of the country's coffee production is exported. The cultivation of coffee is primarily in the southern states of India and depends predominantly on the south west monsoon. Due to the current change in the climate patterns, artificial irrigation is essential to boost the productivity. Various studies have proven that the crop experiences water stress during dry season and this inhibits the blossoming of buds, consequently reducing the yield considerably. Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) assists in monitoring the soil and environmental parameters through appropriate sensors. Soil moisture sensors and soil electrical conductivity sensors can help to detect the water and nutrient deficit in the soil and appropriately apply water and nutrients through drip irrigation system. A leaf wetness sensor can also be used to estimate the transpiration and photosynthesis rate besides predicting the risk of bacterial and fungal attacks. The irrigation can be scheduled and automated based on the prevailing field conditions.

title: A holistic framework for water sustainability and eduction in municipal green spaces
source_title: 2012 25th IEEE Canadian Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Vision for A Greener Future Ccece 2012
title_norm: a holistic framework for water sustainability and eduction in municipal green spaces
abstract: This paper describes an irrigation control system that incorporates wireless soil moisture sensors and real time user feedback. The system is deployed on a large scale in a municipal green space. It is estimated that between 60% to 70% of municipal water is used for irrigation. Current systems struggle to adapt to site specific variations. Our approach augments an existing commercial water budget controller with a wireless soil sensor network and an adaptive irrigation controller to significantly reduce water usage. The system requires less user intervention than today's commercial systems that attempt to offer similar water savings. The community is able to watch dynamic changes in soil moisture and watering so that they can garner a better understanding of patterns of sustainable water use.

title: Innovative Solutions for Water and Energy Challenges in Agriculture: A Review of Solar-Powered Irrigation Systems
source_title: 2023 1st International Conference on Circuits Power and Intelligent Systems Ccpis 2023
title_norm: innovative solutions for water and energy challenges in agriculture a review of solarpowered irrigation systems
abstract: The increasing population in developing countries is putting pressure on the demand for more food production, and modernization efforts are being made in the agricultural sector. In many developing countries, rainwater is heavily relied upon for agricultural practices, but the government and regional authorities have implemented various measures to enhance the accessibility of water for agriculture throughout the year. The majority of farmers depend on groundwater as their main water source, but the increasing prices of fossil fuels and inadequate electric grids in remote areas pose challenges to traditional water pumping methods. One solution to achieving sustainable and profitable agriculture is using renewable energy sources like solar energy for water pumping, which offers advantages such as reduced pollution and no fuel costs in the long term. Developing countries have widely adopted solar pumps, but the success of this technology depends on various elements like climatic conditions, crop type, groundwater availability, government support, and the cost and availability of conventional electricity.

title: Shallot Automated Fertilization and Irrigation Device Using Solar-Powered IoT Based on ESP-NOW and LoRa
source_title: Proceedings of the International Conference on Computer Engineering Network and Intelligent Multimedia Cenim 2024
title_norm: shallot automated fertilization and irrigation device using solarpowered iot based on espnow and lora
abstract: The agricultural industry is a fundamental component of the global economy, essential for maintaining food security for the ever-increasing world population. Shallots are an essential ingredient in numerous cuisines worldwide. This research aims to develop a device that employs an automated irrigation and fertilization system for shallot plants, leveraging the Internet of Things (IoT) powered by solar panels and encompassing ESP-NOW and LoRa communication protocols. This research investigates the application of IoT technology in the automation of fertilization and irrigation via a monitoring system and relay control. Systematic testing methods focused on energy efficiency yield verification through data collection and transmission, demonstrating consistent accuracy of 99.3% for the air humidity sensor, 99.1% for the air temperature sensor, 97% for the soil moisture sensor, and 95.5% for the soil pH sensor. The device uses ESP-NOW for communication between ESP32s and utilizes LoRa for data transmission via the LoRa Gateway endpoint, Antares. This paper presents a solution for automating agricultural practices, proposing a design for an IoT Smart Farming device that employs solar energy and wireless communication protocols for land monitoring and managing irrigation and fertilizer.

source_title: Proceedings 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies Cicn 2024
title_norm: enhancing agricultural efficiency with iotenabled precision irrigation management using lorawan technology
abstract: The Internet of Things-empowered precision irrigation management system with LoRaWAN technology is presented given the growing food requirements across the world and pressing calls for judicious use of water in agriculture. Flow Pilot, specifically designed for chili farms, optimizes water application while enhancing crop health using precise and automated irrigation. title: A Sustainable Solar-Powered IoT and Machine Learning Framework for Smart Agricultural Monitoring
source_title: 2025 17th IEEE International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Communication Networks Cicn 2025
title_norm: a sustainable solarpowered iot and machine learning framework for smart agricultural monitoring
abstract: As food consumption has increased in both quantity and quality, the need for agricultural modernization and intensification has also grown. The Internet of Things (IoT), a promising technology, has enabled various cuttingedge agricultural solutions. Scientific companies and research institutions are continuously working to develop products and services that leverage IoT to address various challenges. The primary aim of this research is to gather extensive knowledge on IoT-based agricultural applications, including sensors/devices, communication protocols, and network designs. In regions where power and water are scarce, developing a solar energy system based on IoT for smart irrigation is crucial. A machine learning-based method was implemented using a Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Cat Swarm Optimization (CSO) to develop an IoT-based solar energy solution for smart farming. By integrating IoT and machine learning with agricultural practices, the proposed system enhances operational effectiveness and efficiency. Sensory systems improve crop monitoring, reduce environmental impact, and promote resource conservation for farmers. These advanced systems enable efficient water management and offer superior soil and weather monitoring capabilities. The proposed SVM-CSO method includes a prediction process in which an IoT-based solar cell supplies the essential operating power. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed solar-powered IoT and SVMCSO framework achieves an accuracy of up to 96.13 %, outperforming other models and thereby enhancing agricultural productivity while reducing energy consumption.

source_title: International Conference on Intelligent Processing Hardware Electronics and Radio Systems Cipher 2026

abstract: This paper describes an IoT-based smart irrigation system to help farmers in field monitoring and water management. It is primarily based on low-cost sensors for measuring the moisture content of the soil, temperature, humidity, and nutrients of the soil, and all these sensors are connected to the ESP32 microcontroller. title: Precision Agriculture: Enhancing Crop Yield and Water Efficiency with Smart Irrigation Systems
source_title: Proceedings 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Sustainable Computational Technologies Cisct 2024
title_norm: precision agriculture enhancing crop yield and water efficiency with smart irrigation systems
abstract: Traditional methods of irrigation can inefficiently use water leading to excess usage and less than ideal crop yield. To tackle this problem, we will employ a smart irrigation system equipped with soil moisture sensors. The system is intended to improve irrigation practices, delivering water more efficiently based on data like soil moisture in real time. An array of soil moisture sensors, located throughout the field are monitoring constantly in real-time at various depths and areas for measuring the content of water present in it. The data was sent to an Arduino board which analyzes the data using some smart algorithms. According to the data evaluated by means of this, the time as well as the type in which irrigation is required for different field areas are determined very carefully via control unit. It activates actuators or valves to control the irrigation system, thus guaranteeing an optimal water distribution when necessary. Not only that but this system can be combined with weather forecasting to calibrate watering schedules considering rainfall or other conditions. The smart irrigation system offers multiple benefits such as: -W ater Management- crop yield increases and resource conservation. EPA has a tailored and responsive irrigation solution, which saves water wastage as well as maintain health for plant growth. This is a sustainable and low-cost solution for modern agriculture that can adjust to different types of soils conditions or environmental changes, becoming an important tool in the arsenal farmers have access.

title: A Hybrid Attention-Based ST-CNN and Penman-Monteith Framework for High-Resolution Soil Moisture Recharge Prediction Using Satellite Driven Data
source_title: 2025 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Computing Applications and Systems Compas 2025
title_norm: a hybrid attentionbased stcnn and penmanmonteith framework for highresolution soil moisture recharge prediction using satellite driven data
abstract: In monsoon-affected tropical deltas such as Bangladesh, where precipitation, evapotranspiration, and anthropogenic use of water combine complexly, accurately predicting soil moisture recharge (SMR) is essential for efficient agricultural water management. Most of the time, conventional procedure-based or machine learning approaches fail to do an adequate job of illustrating how SMR changes over time and space at high resolution. To deal with this problem, we present an innovative hybrid approach that brings together the Penman-Monteith evapotranspiration model with a spatiotemporal convolutional neural network that is based on attention (ST-CNN-Attention). Bangladesh’s all 64 districts have been included in the model, which utilizes the complete NASA POWER dataset encompassing the years 2004–2024. It includes 22 daily climatic and geographic parameters. To maintain the reliability of the hydrological system, it employs CNN-based pattern recognition from satellite data, LSTM networks with attention mechanisms that focus on vital monsoon dynamics, and physically controlled evapotranspiration. This is the very first high-resolution SMR forecast system built specifically for Bangladesh’s predominant polder hydrology. It is more accurate yet simpler to utilize. This structure is versatile so it can be utilized to arrange proper irrigation, alert of droughts ahead of time, and take ways to deal with climate change. Also, it could be beneficial in other delta regions that have been affected by rainfall and have water-management problems that are equivalent to those in the above locations.

source_title: 2017 IEEE 37th Central America and Panama Convention Concapan 2017

abstract: Due to the current climate change, the season and amount of rain in the agricultural zones has varied, frequently causing insufficient water and even drought. It is for this reason that irrigation systems are of great importance to cover the moisture requirements of plants. Among existing irrigation systems, drip irrigation is one of the most used as it can reduce water use, due to its uniformity of application. In this paper one presents the design and development of a drip irrigation system at laboratory level, water is applied near the root zone of a plant in order to maintain a constant humidity for its life cycle. The humidity of the earth near the plant is determined by means of sensors and the necessary hardware is developed for the automatic activation of the water supply by means of pumps, in addition to lighting a visual alarm.

title: Agricultural Management and Remote Monitoring for Carbon Sequestration: The Case of Latin America
source_title: Proceedings of 2024 IEEE Central America and Panama Student Conference Conescapan 2024
title_norm: agricultural management and remote monitoring for carbon sequestration the case of latin america
abstract: Capturing sequestration is a crucial approach to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, particularly carbon dioxide (CO2). This literature review analyzes various agricultural practices and remote monitoring models applied to carbon sequestration in Latin America. It evaluates the impact of practices such as irrigation, organic agriculture, the use of fertilizers and amendments in grasslands, on increasing carbon in the region's soils. Additionally, it studies the application of remote monitoring models such as NDVI, MODIS, RothC and SPOT to collect data through satellite imagery. The results reveal that these agricultural practices and monitoring models are poorly implemented in Latin America. This highlights the importance of promoting their adoption to optimize carbon sequestration in different areas of the region. Greater carbon capture in soils would contribute significantly to mitigating climate change and achieving emission reduction goals. Therefore, it is essential to promote policies and incentives that drive these sustainable practices in the Latin American agricultural sector.

source_title: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Cloud Computing Data Science and Engineering Confluence 2024
title_norm: iot based realtime monitoring system for precision agriculture
abstract: In this paper, Nodemcu ESP8266, an Internet of Things (lOT) based Real time farm monitoring system is considered for real time monitoring. A few agricultural-related problems have always impeded the nation's progress. Thus, smart agriculture-a modernization of the current traditional agricultural methods-is the only way to address this issue. Therefore, Internet of Things based technology is being used to make agriculture smarter. Numerous applications, such as automatic irrigation decision support and crop growth monitoring and selection. In this paper, ESP8266 loT automatic irrigation system is used to update and raise crop productivity. The paper demonstrates how to create loT based Real- time farm monitoring through the use of inexpensive, readily accessible sensors. The capacitive soil moisture sensor is utilized to determine the moisture in the soil. For measuring humidity and air temperature, DHTII Humidity Temperature Sensor is used. Further, a 5V power relay will be used to run the water pump. Whenever the sensor detects that there is insufficient moisture in the soil, the motor turns on automatically and irrigate the field. The motor shuts off as soon as the soil gets wet. With the help of thing speak server online, you can remotely watch all of this from anywhere in the world.

title: Smart Irrigation System for Roses: Enhancing Sustainable Production in Greenhouses through Industry 4.0 and Digital Technologies
source_title: Congreso Internacional De Innovacion Y Tendencias En Ingenieria Coniiti
title_norm: smart irrigation system for roses enhancing sustainable production in greenhouses through industry 40 and digital technologies
abstract: Greenhouse rose production is often affected by inefficient manual irrigation systems, resulting in excessive water consumption and inconsistent flower quality. This research presents the design and validation of a smart irrigation system that integrates Industry 4.0 digital technologies such as IoT sensors, cloud computing, and adaptive control algorithms. The system monitors soil moisture and environmental variables in real time, enabling precise and efficient water application only when necessary. Implemented in a prototype greenhouse, the solution achieved a 32% reduction in water use while maintaining optimal plant growth. The study highlights the potential of data-driven rule-based control (with AI planned), data driven irrigation automation to improve sustainability, reduce human error, and increase productivity in ornamental horticulture, especially for rose growers in developing countries. This approach can be replicated for other ornamental crops and greenhouse settings in water scarce environments.

title: Irrigation Optimization in Agricultural Fields Using Deep Reinforcement Learning Approaches
source_title: 2025 29th International Computer Conference Computer Society of Iran Csicc 2025
title_norm: irrigation optimization in agricultural fields using deep reinforcement learning approaches
abstract: In recent years, due to the world population growth, the demand for agricultural products has also increased. Global crises such as climate change, destruction of water resources, pollution and destruction of aquatic ecosystems, have limited the access to clean water to irrigate the agricultural fields in a global scale. Meanwhile, according to the reports of Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), about 70% of global water consumption is allocated to agricultural activities. Therefore, it is necessary to minimize water consumption during agricultural irrigation while maximizing crop yield by the end of the season. Most IoT frameworks used in irrigation systems collect data from the soil and weather, then send it to the user, leaving the final decision on irrigation to the user. This approach may cause water wastage or even water stress for the plants as the amount of water irrigated in fields may be low. In this paper, we will use deep reinforcement learning approaches to reach this goal. We propose a novel approach to minimize water usage while keeping the yield produced at the highest level. Our approach utilizes DQN and A2C networks. The findings demonstrate that our methods reduce water wastage compared to previous approaches, making it more flexible and practical in varying weather and soil conditions.

title: A Sustainable Smart Irrigation and Crop Protection System for Bangladesh
source_title: 8th IEEE International Conference on Computational System and Information Technology for Sustainable Solutions Csitss 2024
title_norm: a sustainable smart irrigation and crop protection system for bangladesh
abstract: Bangladesh's most crucial sector for development is agriculture. Rainfall has been irregular in recent years due to climate change. In our country, the untimely rain and hailstorms harm crops and vegetables, especially winter vegetables. Surface water is mainly used for agriculture, but its availability constantly declines. Our current key challenge is to save surface water while protecting crops from rain and hail. IoT is cutting-edge technology in many applications, such as smart homes, smart cities, and intelligent traffic management. The IoT may be implemented in so many different industries and sectors. This research work is about smart irrigation with crop protection systems in agriculture. The system's primary parts are the sensors, water pump, servo motors, embedded systems, and internet connectivity. IoT sensors like soil moisture sensors and rain sensors are used in the suggested methodology. The fields of crops have received water from a pump. A motor has covered the crops. The proposed solution is a straightforward Internet of Things setup that sends data to the Arduino after detecting rainfall and soil moisture levels. Depending on the sensor data, the Arduino sends signals to the motor and pump to irrigate the crops and cover crops as necessary, revealing the crops after rain. The system is constructed economically using bamboo, and poly and plastic nets have been utilized to protect the crops from rain and fog. The system's primary effects are increased productivity, decreased crop damage rate, and saved surface water.

Further integration of fog computing with machine learning will bring more developments to smart agriculture systems. The system is integrated into fog computing and machine learning to manage real-time data processing to achieve faster and more accurate predictions.

title: A Dataset for IoT-Enabled Smart Irrigation Using UAVs for Multispectral Sensing in Agriculture
source_title: 2026 IEEE 15th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies Csnt 2026
title_norm: a dataset for iotenabled smart irrigation using uavs for multispectral sensing in agriculture
abstract: Precision Agriculture (PA) can help reduce water consumption in dry regions, yet many PA systems still rely on cloud-based processing. This dependence introduces latency and requires stable internet connectivity, which is often unavailable in rural environments. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) offer high spatial resolution compared to satellite platforms; however, most UAV-based approaches depend on computationally intensive deep learning (DL) models that are unsuitable for real-time execution on edge devices. title: IrrNet: Advancing Irrigation Mapping with Incremental Patch Size Training on Remote Sensing Imagery
source_title: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops
title_norm: irrnet advancing irrigation mapping with incremental patch size training on remote sensing imagery
abstract: Irrigation mapping plays a crucial role in effective water management, essential for preserving both water quality and quantity, and is key to mitigating the global issue of water scarcity. The complexity of agricultural fields, adorned with diverse irrigation practices, especially when multiple systems coexist in close quarters, poses a unique challenge. This complexity is further compounded by the nature of Landsat’s remote sensing data, where each pixel is rich with densely packed information, complicating the task of accurate irrigation mapping. In this study, we introduce an innovative approach that employs a progressive training method, which strategically increases patch sizes throughout the training process, utilizing datasets from Landsat 5 and 7, labeled with the WRLU dataset for precise labeling. This initial focus allows the model to capture detailed features, progressively shifting to broader, more general features as the patch size enlarges. Remarkably, our method enhances the performance of existing state-of-the-art models by approximately 20%. Furthermore, our analysis delves into the significance of incorporating various spectral bands into the model, assessing their impact on performance. The findings reveal that additional bands are instrumental in enabling the model to discern finer details more effectively. This work sets a new standard for leveraging remote sensing imagery in irrigation mapping.

title: A combination of multi and univariate anomaly detection in urban irrigation systems
source_title: 2022 3rd International Conference on Embedded and Distributed Systems Edis 2022
title_norm: a combination of multi and univariate anomaly detection in urban irrigation systems
abstract: Water scarcity is a global concern that requires a more intelligent way to manage the water network in order to minimize consumption and losses. There is a current need for new automated and intelligent decision support systems that employ data analytic advances to analyze in real-time the anomalies and problems that appear in water usage. In our case, we have developed a 3 steps system using unsupervised algorithms, that has been tested on the irrigation of urban parks. Those steps consist of grouping the parks according to similarities in the irrigation by clustering the consumption time series, searching for the dates where multivariate anomalies occur in every group using the Vector Autoregressive Model, and finally, applying an ARIMA framework to each series in the area of those dates. Our methodology reduces the time that anomaly detection univariate systems require for analysing the whole univariate time series by extracting previous knowledge on a multivariate approach. This methodology, when integrated with an IoT platform, is a tool for easing the labelling of real anomalies and can help create supervised datasets for future research in the area. The approach is used in urban scenarios, however, can easily be extended to be an application for smart agriculture scenarios.

title: Virtual Sensor for Efficient Soil Fertilizer and Water Content Differentiation
source_title: Proceedings of Edis 2024 2024 4th International Conference on Embedded and Distributed Systems
title_norm: virtual sensor for efficient soil fertilizer and water content differentiation
abstract: Soil degradation issues, such as salinization, waterlogging, and erosion, pose significant challenges in agricultural irrigation and fertigation. Conventional laboratory methods for analyzing soil conditions are often cost-prohibitive, time-intensive, and require specialized personnel. This study investigates the application of a virtual sensor, incorporating RGB and LDR modules, to measure fertilizer concentration and water content in soil, as well as to differentiate between water and fertilizer. Statistical analysis of the acquired data using ANOVA revealed significant differences between samples under blue, yellow, and magenta lights, with p-values of 0.0425, 0.018, and 0.0425, respectively. Machine Learning (ML) techniques were employed to enhance the system's performance, yielding an 87.5% accuracy in binary classification using the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and Euclidean models. Additionally, regression models demonstrated R2 values of 0.802 and 0.891 for irrigated and ferti-irrigated soils, respectively. These results suggest that the proposed optical sensor system is a promising, cost-effective alternative to traditional methods, though further validation in real-world applications is necessary.

title: On the Laminar Flow Regime Forming in Pipelines for Drip Irrigation
source_title: 2022 8th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering EE and Ae 2022 Proceedings
title_norm: on the laminar flow regime forming in pipelines for drip irrigation
abstract: Under the new conditions of agricultural development and water resources, it is necessary to take into account the fact that the our country has a limited water resources, distributed unevenly over its territory. For this reason, water now appears as a limiting factor and becomes extremely important from an environmental and economic point of view. Saving irrigation water can be achieved by using efficient methods such as drip irrigation. In order to clarify the problem of sustainable use of water for irrigation, it is necessary to analyze the hydraulic and energy-efficient characteristics of water movement in irrigation systems and the conditions under which its transport and distribution to agricultural crops takes place. In the case of polyethylene - PE irrigation laterals for drip irrigation, a water quantity is consumed along their length. Under this condition, the flow rate gradually decreases and this leads to the formation of different flow regimes along the pipeline. In the present study, the question of the length of the part of the PE pipeline with laminar regime is considered, as well as the conditions predetermining the onset of this regime in PE pipelines ф 16/2 and ф 20/2. The conditions depend on the number of water localized outfalls, i.e. drippers, the magnitude of their flow rate, and the distance between them for a given assumed inner diameter and water temperature.

title: NLP - Bayesian Network Framework - Integrating Scientific Knowledge and Data-Driven Models into Sustainable Turf Management Decision Support System
source_title: 2025 10th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering EE and Ae 2025 Conference Proceedings
title_norm: nlp  bayesian network framework  integrating scientific knowledge and datadriven models into sustainable turf management decision support system
abstract: Sustainable turfgrass management requires decisions that account for uncertainty in weather, soil processes, and human practices, yet the underlying scientific knowledge is fragmented across disciplines. This study presents a probabilistic framework that integrates Natural Language Processing (NLP), Machine Learning (ML), and Bayesian Networks (BN) to combine literature-derived causal knowledge with site-specific turfgrass data. Using transformer-based extraction, scientific publications were converted into structured causal relations, which were then merged with empirical observations from IoT sensors, remote sensing, and ML models. A pilot implementation focused on nitrogen fertilization and irrigation. The BN generated site-specific recommendations that reduced irrigation needs by 14.9% while maintaining a 98% probability of acceptable turf quality, and enabled 25% lower nitrogen inputs with an estimated 12% probability of over-fertilization risk. Integrating literature priors with real-time data improved interpretability of ML outputs and allowed explicit intervention queries relevant to management practice. The modular structure enables extension to additional management domains and other environmental systems. The results demonstrate that combining causal knowledge extraction with dynamic probabilistic modelling can support more efficient and transparent decision-making in turfgrass management.

title: Methodology for Improving Soil Conditions of Meadows and Pastures Through the Application of Alternative Technology
source_title: 2025 10th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering EE and Ae 2025 Conference Proceedings
title_norm: methodology for improving soil conditions of meadows and pastures through the application of alternative technology
abstract: Pasture is an agricultural area, overgrown mainly with herbaceous vegetation, intended for grazing domestic or wild animals. Unlike meadows, which are mainly used for mowing and harvesting hay, pastures are used directly as a source of fodder through grazing. They are characterized by natural or sown herbage, a permanent purpose for animal husbandry and have an important role in maintaining biodiversity and soil fertility. Improving soil conditions on a pasture is key to better productivity and sustainability. It can be achieved through the following practices: application of organic and mineral fertilizers, deep cultivation and avoidance of compaction, drainage and irrigation of the terrain. Alternative technology is such technology that differs from conventional or traditional methods of production, processing, or management and offers a different approach to achieve the same or better goal. This is achieved through the application of greener, energy-efficient and innovative or non-traditional methods. This article aims to offer a variant of technology through the use of modern methods of pasture diagnostics and to apply fundamentally new machines to improve soil conditions. In this article, the alternative processing machines are an agricultural robot and a drone. The drone is a product of the XAG company, and the robot is a development of the Agricultural University - Plovdiv. The technology was tested on experimental pasture of 5 ha in Agricultural University - Plovdiv, and no comparison was made with the conventional. Fertilization with the drone takes about 1 h with the additional charging time, and fertilization with the robot takes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2 h 1 0 ~ m i n}$</tex>. Aeration of the soil with the robot on the experimental pasture takes 20 h.

title: AI-Driven Dynamic Water Resource Prediction and Optimization Algorithms for Precision Irrigation
source_title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Electronics Energy Systems and Power Engineering Eespe 2025
title_norm: aidriven dynamic water resource prediction and optimization algorithms for precision irrigation
abstract: Addressing the escalating global scarcity of water resources and the pressing need for efficient irrigation in agricultural production, this research introduces a novel AI-powered framework for dynamic water resource prediction and optimization tailored for precision irrigation [1]. This framework innovatively integrates advanced machine learning techniques to achieve accurate, real-time forecasting of farmland water demand and subsequently optimizes irrigation strategies based on these predictions. Distinct from conventional approaches relying on static or simplified models, this study innovatively fuses multi-source heterogeneous information, including meteorological data, soil moisture levels, and crop growth stages, to construct a deep learning-based time-series forecasting model[2]. This model effectively captures the non-linear dynamic characteristics of water resource requirements. Furthermore, we designed a reinforcement learning-based irrigation decision optimization algorithm capable of dynamically adjusting irrigation parameters based on the predictive outcomes and real-time environmental feedback. This approach aims to minimize water consumption while concurrently maximizing crop yield. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly surpasses traditional methods in water resource prediction accuracy. Moreover, in practical irrigation scenarios, it effectively enhances water utilization efficiency, boosts crop productivity, and reduces energy expenditure, thereby providing robust technological support for sustainable agricultural development. This research exhibits significant innovation in both algorithm design and system integration, effectively overcoming the limitations of existing precision irrigation technologies regarding dynamic environmental adaptability and intelligent decision-making capabilities.

title: Implementing a Smart Irrigation System using IoT Technology to Achieve Saudi's Green Ambition
source_title: 2023 IEEE 7th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration Ei2 2023
title_norm: implementing a smart irrigation system using iot technology to achieve saudis green ambition
abstract: With the global rise in population and the consequential surge in demand for agricultural products, efficient water management has become imperative to sustain agricultural practices. In arid regions like Saudi Arabia, where water scarcity poses a significant challenge to agriculture, adopting smart irrigation systems integrated with Internet of Things (IoT) technology emerges as a promising solution. This study explores the implementation of a Smart Irrigation System (SIS) utilizing IoT technology to align with Saudi Arabia's ambitious goals of environmental sustainability and agricultural self-sufficiency. Methods: The proposed system uses a microprocessor that leverages IoT devices such as soil moisture sensors, salinity sensors, ultrasonic sensors, water pumps, and automated actuators to create an intelligent, data-driven irrigation framework. Real-time data from these sensors were collected and analysed using algorithms to determine precise irrigation requirements based on factors like soil moisture levels, weather conditions, and crop types. By integrating IoT technology, the system facilitates remote monitoring and control through a userfriendly interface accessible via smartphones or computers. This seamless integration of digital technologies optimizes water usage, reduces wastage, and enhances overall agricultural productivity. The prototype explained the methods trial data were collected and the results are promising. Also, the statistical analysis was achieved. Results: The proposed system displays data from moisture and TDS soil sensors. The ultrasonic distance sensor detects the water level in a tank, and the pump waters the plants when the soil moisture is low. Finally, an IoT module was integrated with these sensors to send notifications wirelessly via Wi-Fi or GSM to the user or farmer. The system can control and monitoring in real time. ANOVA statistical analysis indicates a significant difference with p <.05 in the correlations between salinity, TDS, moisture, and water respectively. measurements. That means the study can have success if applied on a larger scale. Conclusion: The project represents a transformative approach toward achieving Saudi Arabia's green ambition. By harnessing the power of data-driven decision-making, this innovative solution not only addresses the pressing issue of water scarcity but also fosters sustainable agriculture, economic growth, and environmental preservation, thus paving the way for a greener and more prosperous future and in line with the Kingdom Vision 2030.

title: Sustainable Smart Irrigation in Precision Farming using IoT
source_title: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics Esci 2025
title_norm: sustainable smart irrigation in precision farming using iot
abstract: The current paper applies computational models based on machine intelligence to enhance the application of water in precision agriculture. This is to establish a reliable tool that can predict the most appropriate ambience of watering, hence enhancing sustainability. It includes what is referred to as sensor integration, and the establishment of a wireless sensor network (WSN). It gives analysis of a well-chosen data log containing essential sensor values like soil moisture, rain, humidity, wind speed and temperature. This paper work elaborates stages of Signal pre-processing, signal conditioning, training and testing performed for available stored dataset. Through the given 105,217 record dataset, smart irrigation accuracy compared using the support vector machine (SVM), random forest, decision tree, artificial neural network as well as other machine learning modes. Database are first trained then evaluated and finally samples are tested. The results of the current study depict that the random forest model is comparatively accurate than the other models with an accuracy of 92.68%. The second best performing method, which is only marginally less accurate than the random forest is decision Trees, with a success rate of 91.83%. SVM and neural network models also gave fairly good performance with accuracy of 90.78 and 90.21 respectively. The random forest model’s accuracy in forecasting ideal irrigation conditions which is further supported by the precision along with F1-Score measures. This paper provides a strong foundation for environmentally friendly water use and offers insightful information about using machine learning techniques for precision agriculture

source_title: Esic 2025 5th International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing Proceedings
title_norm: classification algorithms for pump control as well as multiobjective optimization for pump scheduling
abstract: Over or undersupply of water will negatively impact crop health. A Smart Irrigation system is the need of the hour in agriculture technology which can optimize water use and enhance crop health for sustainable and precision farming promoting higher yields. IoT and AI-driven systems are more efficient than a simple automated system by reducing water and power wastage. Our system leverages IoT devices such as capacitive soil moisture sensors and DHT-11 sensors. Our system predicts pump activation status (binary classification: pump on/off) based on environmental features. title: Synthesis of AI-Driven Integrated Solar Energy and Smart Irrigation Systems for Climate-Smart Tropical Agriculture
source_title: Esic 2026 Proceedings 6th International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing
title_norm: synthesis of aidriven integrated solar energy and smart irrigation systems for climatesmart tropical agriculture
abstract: Climate variability, increasing water scarcity and instability of conventional electricity supply exert considerable pressure on tropical agricultural systems. Solar irrigation has become a practical and environmentally friendly alternative to diesel pumps and grid-connected energy sources. Despite their potential, the performance of PV systems in tropical environments is often limited by adverse environmental conditions. High temperatures, significant particulate deposits and persistent humidity jointly degrade PV conversion performance, resulting in energy losses of about 15-25% during peaks in solar demand [1], [2]. These losses decrease the overall efficiency and reliability of solarpowered irrigation system, especially during critical period of irrigation. Consequently, advances in smart irrigation, particularly use of Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, AI, and geospatial monitoring, has reduced water consumption by 40% while improving productivity [6], [7]. Nevertheless, there are currently few systematic assessments in the context of tropical agriculture, and research on the integration of solar irrigation with AI control is still lacking. This review suggests that AI-driven solar-powered irrigation systems could significantly improve resource-use efficiency and provide resilience in climate-smart agriculture, but scaling requires standardization of performance metrics, multi-site testing, and inclusive funding strategies.

title: AgroInnovate: A Framework for Sustainable and Smart Irrigation in Agriculture
source_title: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications Gcitc 2023
title_norm: agroinnovate a framework for sustainable and smart irrigation in agriculture
abstract: Agriculture is a fundamental global practice, reliant on optimal conditions for crop productivity. Agriculture, a globally embraced practice, demands optimal conditions for efficient crop production and yield improvement. This research introduces an intelligent irrigation monitoring and control system, employing Internet of Things (IoT) technology. The system leverages soil pH, moisture, and temperature data obtained from field sensors, storing it in the cloud. It allows manual and automated operation via a mobile app, with automated mode activating pumps based on soil conditions. Key parameters, including soil pH, moisture, and temperature, are sensed using on-field sensors, with data stored in the cloud. The system introduces dual operational modes, manual and automated, to cater to varying farmer requirements. In manual mode, farmers retain remote control, enabling the activation or deactivation of critical components such as the water motor pump, water sprinkler pump, and fertilizer pump, all via a user-friendly mobile application. In automated mode, pumps are triggered based on soil conditions, optimizing water and fertilizer use. The system also maintains ideal soil pH, promoting crop growth. Additionally, it manages soil pH by automatically adjusting fertilizer injection. The proposed system offers remote monitoring and control via a website or mobile app, aiming to maximize crop production while adhering to standard parameters. This research proposes a sensor module for parameter measurement and actuation. The system facilitates remote monitoring and control through a website or mobile app, aiming to maximize crop production while adhering to standard parameters. Upon detecting soil conditions falling outside the predefined threshold values, the system initiates automatic control actions. When soil moisture registers below the established threshold, the system automatically activates the water supply pump to ensure adequate irrigation. Conversely, when the soil temperature surpasses the defined threshold, the system triggers the water sprinkle pump to mitigate excessive heat and optimize crop growth conditions. This dynamic response mechanism, orchestrated by the automated mode, serves as an indispensable feature of the proposed system, enhancing its ability to provide timely and precise irrigation support based on real-time soil conditions.

title: Towards Hybrid Smart Irrigation for Mixed-Cropping
source_title: 2022 Global Conference on Wireless and Optical Technologies Gcwot 2022
title_norm: towards hybrid smart irrigation for mixedcropping
abstract: Agricultural countries are facing water shortage problems. Due to mismanagement of the water distribution system and selection of inappropriate irrigation methods, water could be over-utilized that will affect crop production. Consequently, the economy of these countries could be badly affected. Moreover, water shortage problems also occur and the agriculturists bear financial losses as a result of this water scarcity. Existing irrigation systems are designed for specific crops cultivated in a season but that is not useful for other crops planned to be grown in the next season. Currently, the practice of mixed cropping is being used in the same agricultural field to gain more income in which farmers are growing vegetables with regular crops. For this practice, computerized systems are required for water scheduling among both crops. To cope up with these challenges, several Irrigation systems i.e. using WSN s, cloud-based, rule mining based and mobile-oriented solutions using GPRS have been proposed in the literature. These systems are functioning on unidirectional data focusing on a single irrigation system at a time, hence are unable to address factual solutions. There is a fundamental need to develop smart context-aware irrigation systems with the ability to deal with multi-cropping/mixed cropping in a particular field. In this paper, a smart context-aware irrigation system has been presented to deploy automated hybrid irrigation methods for mixed cropping practices to achieve more yield production. The system entails three maj or parts: 1) WSN s based data acquirement systems, 2) Decision Supports System and 3) Context-aware water scheduling. This system will help farmers in intensive farming of mixed cropping and cultivate large areas with less amount of water by applying three standard methods of irrigation according to the type and requirements of crops, land condition/soil types with context-awareness.

title: IoT Sensor Network Approach for Smart Farming: An Application in Food, Energy and Water System
source_title: Ghtc 2018 IEEE Global Humanitarian Technology Conference Proceedings
title_norm: iot sensor network approach for smart farming an application in food energy and water system
abstract: As the global population soars from today's 7.3 billion to an estimated 10 billion by 2050, the demand for Food, Energy and Water (FEW) is expected to more than double. Such an increase in population and consequently, in the demand for FEW resources will undoubtedly be a great challenge for humankind. A challenge that will be exacerbated by the need for humankind to meet the greater demand for resources with a smaller ecological footprint. This paper is proposing a system developed to optimize the use of water, energy, fertilizers for agricultural crops as a solution to this great challenge. It is an automated smart irrigation system that uses real time data from wireless sensor networks to schedule an irrigation. The test-bed consists of a wireless network monitoring soil moisture, temperature, solar radiation, humidity, and fertilizer sensors embedded in the root area of the crops and around the test-bed. Wireless sensor data transmission and acquisition is managed by an Access Point (AP) using ZigBee protocol. An algorithm was established based on threshold values of temperature and soil moisture automated into a programmable micro-controller to control irrigation time. The system's energy demand is completely supplied by a solar Photo-voltaic (PV) panel supplemented with an energy storage unit. The experimental data obtained from this prototype will be modeled and optimized to investigate food production profile as a function of energy and water consumption. It will also attempt to understand the effect of extreme weather conditions on food production. This holistic approach will explore the nexus between water and energy resources, and crop yield for several essential crops in an attempt to design a more sustainable method to meet the forecasted surge in demand.

title: Monitoring the Impacts of Disruption Events on Agriculture Through Irrigation Detection with Remote Sensing
source_title: 2024 IEEE Global Humanitarian Technology Conference Ghtc 2024
title_norm: monitoring the impacts of disruption events on agriculture through irrigation detection with remote sensing
abstract: Adoption of irrigation even on a small scale requires access to suitable soils, sourcing seeds and fertilizers, meeting crop water requirements, energy and infrastructure needed for pumping water and access to markets. Therefore monitoring irrigation over time provides key insight on the effectiveness of policy decisions, infrastructure successes and more importantly, disruptions caused by events such as conflicts, the COVID pandemic etc. All of these have a direct impact on food security. However most of the irrigation maps including coarse global irrigation cropland layers are created for a certain time period and do not reflect changes in the landscape over time. This study presents a simplified alternative to a dry season irrigation detection methodology developed for the Ethiopian highlands that can be implemented using Google Earth Engine's built in classifiers to create irrigation maps for each year of interest. The original methodology and the proposed simplified approach are compared for a sample region in Oromia to discuss the trade-offs of the simplifications. It is then applied to Southern Tigray across five years from 2019 to 2023 to show how the monitoring technique can be used to visualize the effects of disruptions such as the Tigray War on irrigated agriculture and the recovery efforts after.

title: AI-Driven Short-Term Solar PV Forecasting for Smart Agricultural Irrigation Systems Using a Novel Hybrid Machine Learning Model
source_title: 2025 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies Giest 2025
title_norm: aidriven shortterm solar pv forecasting for smart agricultural irrigation systems using a novel hybrid machine learning model
abstract: Integrating solar photovoltaic (PV) systems with smart agricultural irrigation systems is now being considered as a sustainable effort for water and energy management in rural and remote areas. However, the irregularity and instability of solar power, especially in very local time scales (5-60 minutes), often leads to a loss of expected power availability, which makes field irrigation operations difficult. Therefore, accurate very small-term solar PV output estimation is of great importance. In this research paper, a novel and integrated machine learning approach is proposed, which combines CEEMDAN (Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise), Transformer Network, and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) for very small-term estimation of solar PV output. Using CEEMDAN, the signal is divided into several underlying mode functions (IMFs), which facilitate trend analysis of unstable and nonlinear PV data. The Transformer model can capture long-term trends using self-adaptation mechanisms, whereas LightGBM can learn an infinite number of linear links very quickly. These estimates are integrated with a smart irrigation decision support system, which determines the irrigation time and duration based on the available energy and crop water requirements. In the experimental results using a real-world data set based on natural environment data, the proposed method shows significant improvements in the estimation accuracy and irrigation efficiency. This framework makes a significant contribution to building an automated, adaptive, and sustainable agricultural system.

title: Data-Driven Irrigation Optimization: Comparative Study of ML and DL Models
source_title: 2025 International Conference on Next Generation of Green Information and Emerging Technologies Giet 2025
title_norm: datadriven irrigation optimization comparative study of ml and dl models
abstract: Effective management of water resources plays a vital role in achieving sustainable agricultural practices, particularly in the face of increasing climate variability and rising water scarcity. This paper examines the use of artificial intelligence approaches, particularly ML and DL for predicting agricultural water demands. A comprehensive evaluation was conducted using various models including traditional ML algorithms (Random Forest, XGBoost, SVR), deep learning architectures (CNN, RNN, LSTM) and hybrid approaches (LSTM+CNN, RF+XGB). Assessment criteria included statistical indicators like MAE, MSE, MAPE and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to determine how well each model predicted the output. Among all, the LSTM+CNN hybrid model emerged as the top performer, demonstrating superior accuracy and robustness. A multi-criteria decision-making approach using the TOPSIS method further confirmed its effectiveness. The findings highlight the potential of integrating hybrid models with smart irrigation systems to support precision agriculture and ensure sustainable water usage.

title: Innovative Farming with Real-Time Internet of Things Data Classification using Machine Learning and Sensor Networks
source_title: 2025 Global Conference in Emerging Technology Ginotech 2025
title_norm: innovative farming with realtime internet of things data classification using machine learning and sensor networks
abstract: Sustainable agriculture is rapidly rising and being integrated into farming practices through IoT and ML techniques due to the aforementioned global demands. Our study aims to devise an advanced farming system that utilizes real-time IoT data classification for efficient agricultural processes through machine learning algorithms using sensor networks. IoT-based sensor networks allow for the continuous monitoring of different environmental parameters such as soil moisture, temperature, humidity, and crop health, producing large volumes of data. This data is classified and analyzed in real-time using machine learning algorithms, enabling accurate decision-making and automation in farming processes. Data is processed and analyzed on these factors which aids in actionable insights that can help farmers to make better decisions in irrigation management, crop disease detection and yield prediction. The approach of Machine Learning is used to implement these advanced ML models like random forest, support vector machine (SVM), well deep learning neural networks can extract patterns and trends in data which are often missed by previous methods. Enabling predictive analytics through the integration of these technologies allows for proactive measures to adjust to changes in conditions, resulting in improved crop yields and resource utilization. The finding of this study showcases the possible role of IoT and ML in revolutionizing traditional farming practices to minimize the waste of resources, maximize output of harvest and promote sustainability. Moreover, it emphasizes the need for real time data processing as a requirement for modern agriculture that can lead to smart farming systems to fulfil food growth challenges posed by climate change, diminishing agricultural land and increasing food demand. Machine learning-based smart IoT solutions (or comprehensive solutions with IoT solutions) play an important role in the future of agriculture and could contribute to large-scale implementation in many farming scenarios around the world.

title: Land Use Changes Prediction in the Phra Phimon Irrigation Scheme Using Multi-Temporal Landsat Imagery and CA-ANN Model
source_title: 2024 Geoinformatics for Spatial Infrastructure Development in Earth and Allied Sciences GIS Ideas 2024
title_norm: land use changes prediction in the phra phimon irrigation scheme using multitemporal landsat imagery and caann model
abstract: This study analyzes land use changes in the Phra Phimon Operation and Maintenance Project, a large irrigation scheme near Bangkok, Thailand, where rapid urbanization has led to significant modifications in land use and agricultural activities. Landsat satellite imagery from 1993, 2006, and 2019 was used to classify land use into four categories: paddy fields, orchards, urban areas, and water bodies. Future land use changes for 2032 and 2045 were predicted using the CA-Markov coupled with the ANN model (CA-ANN), implemented through QGIS's MOLUSCE plugin. Land use classification achieved 90.95% accuracy (F1-score: 0.91), and prediction accuracy was 67.84% (F1-score: 0.67). Results show significant urban expansion, with urban areas projected to increase from 23.65% in 2019 to 34.87% in 2045, while agricultural areas decrease from 73.28% to 62.00%. This urban growth may result in agricultural land fragmentation, decreased water distribution efficiency, and potential irrigation canal deterioration. This research provides insights for irrigation scheme managers to prepare for future water requirements and infrastructure management changes.

title: A Real Time IoT Machine Learning Pipeline for Tomato Crop Disease Detection Irrigation Optimization and Yield Prediction
source_title: Proceeding of International Conference on Computing Communication Control and Cyber Physical Systems I5cps 2026
title_norm: a real time iot machine learning pipeline for tomato crop disease detection irrigation optimization and yield prediction
abstract: The requirement for food on a global scale and the unstable climatic conditions have shifted agriculture towards a more capable, data-driven method of doing things. A real-time IoT-Machine Learning pipeline for tomato cultivation is outlined in this paper, combining intelligent irrigation control, early disease detection, and analytical yield prediction into a single precision-farming framework. The Internet of Things (IoT) layer consists of soil moisture, temperature, and pressure sensors that help in monitoring the field conditions around the clock, and this is the basis for the automated irrigation that uses solenoid valves powered by a solar-based energy module. In addition to the sensor data, weather forecasts are used to optimize water delivery and reduce wastage. Additionally, the use of Machine Learning model that has been trained with tomato leaf disease datasets is now able to classify pests and pathogens in real-time, which facilitates early intervention and hence, less crop loss. A mathematical yield estimation module takes into account the germination rate, plant density, pest severity index, and water-stress deviation to provide figures for ideal yield, adjusted yield, loss percentages, and total crop productivity. These metrics along with water requirements and market value predictions are visualized through a mobile app and web dashboard, enabling farmers to make informed, evidence-based decisions. The proposed system demonstrates how IoT sensing, automated actuation, and ML-driven analytics can collectively enhance crop health, optimize water usage, minimize economic loss, and move traditional farming towards a more sustainable, efficient, and resilient agricultural model.

title: Effective utilization of embedded system and sensors with Wireless data monitoring for investigation of irrigation scheduling for Sugarcane crop
source_title: 2024 1st International Conference on Cognitive Green and Ubiquitous Computing IC Cgu 2024
title_norm: effective utilization of embedded system and sensors with wireless data monitoring for investigation of irrigation scheduling for sugarcane crop
abstract: In this advanced technological era, farming methods and techniques also get upgraded to improve their yield so that farmers' profits improve. Precision farming uses drip irrigation techniques to optimize its resource utilization. Different technologies like the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), Sensors, and drones bring precise data that helps farmers better schedule and manage. This research paper aims to implement a sensor-based system that optimizes the irrigation schedule for Sugarcane crops in Satara, Maharashtra. In this research, two stages of sugarcane cultivation, i.e., Grand growth and maturation phases, are being monitored. Using a moisture sensor, real-time data is stored through a Wifi module, which determines the theoretical irrigation requirement using the Crop Water Requirement model. The theoretical irrigation requirement is compared with the current irrigation schedule. The study gives insights related to water requirements in different growth stages. During research, the Grand growth phase has a deficit of water as per their requirement. So, the irrigation schedule needs to be closely monitored with exact requirements that optimize the water resource. Conversely, the Maturation phase demonstrated a harmonious alignment between the irrigation schedule and crop water requirements. The research underscores the significance of precision irrigation with drip strategies attuned to specific growth stages for enhancing sugarcane yields. This study showcases the potential of sensor-driven monitoring and data-driven decisions to elevate agricultural practices, ensuring optimal water supply during pivotal growth periods and enhancing overall productivity and resource efficiency. The findings have implications for sustainable agricultural practices and contribute to advancing precision farming techniques.

title: EcoStream SmartFlow System
source_title: 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Information Technology and Engineering Ic Etite 2024
title_norm: ecostream smartflow system
abstract: Agriculture, the backbone of our food supply, faces increasingly daunting challenges due to changing climate patterns and water scarcity. The efficient utilization of water resources has become paramount to ensure sustainable food production while conserving this precious commodity. This project introduces a Smart Irrigation System designed to address these challenges by harnessing the power of temperature and humidity sensors. The core concept of this system is to provide an intelligent, automated solution for delivering the right amount of water to crops precisely when they need it. This is achieved through the integration of sensors that continuously monitor the surrounding environment. Specifically, temperature and humidity sensors are strategically placed in the agricultural field. The signal serves as a trigger for a microcontroller, the brain of the system. By responding to real-time environmental cues, the system ensures that water is delivered only when necessary, eliminating the inefficiencies associated with scheduled irrigation or manual monitoring. The benefits of this Smart Irrigation. Moreover, by responding dynamically to changing conditions, it enhances crop health and yield, ultimately improving the economic viability of agriculture. In conclusion, this project represents a technological leap towards sustainable and efficient agriculture. By incorporating temperature and humidity sensors into the irrigation process, it empowers farmers to adapt to a changing climate, conserve water, and increase their agricultural output. This Smart Irrigation System holds the promise of transforming traditional farming practices into smart, resource-efficient, and environmentally responsible endeavors.

title: Improving the Growth of Jowar Millets in the Region of Uttar Pradesh Using Machine Learning and IoT
source_title: 2024 International Conference on Computer Electronics Electrical Engineering and their Applications Ic2e3 2024
title_norm: improving the growth of jowar millets in the region of uttar pradesh using machine learning and iot
abstract: Agriculture is the main driver of the Indian economy, and technology is transforming conventional farming to increase productivity while reducing resource waste. Water scarcity is the biggest problem facing the globe today, mostly affecting the agricultural system. Consequently, a unique approach is taken while implementing the technology to increase agricultural output. This study aims to develop a smart irrigation system that utilises machine learning enabled by the Internet of Things (IoT) to automatically water plants and notify the user when needed. We have examined the jowar millets' development pattern in the Rampur region of Uttar Pradesh when there is a water shortage. Though it is grown south of Vindhyas, we have used our suggested model in this area because it requires little water. The gathered data is received by a cloud-based server, which saves it, interprets it, and applies machine learning to make irrigation recommendations. Field sensors are used in this project and the data they collect is stored on a cloud server. When deciding how much water to deliver, a decision-making tool called SVM is employed. SVM considers both soil moisture content and ambient temperature while determining how much water to disperse. With an accuracy rate of 99.8%, the SVM classifier is the best; it is closely followed by the RVM classifier, which has an accuracy rating of 98.8%. By contrasting each recommended strategy with earlier research, its efficacy is verified. Based on recognised performance indicators, the experimental results show that the recommended strategy performs better than comparable approaches.

title: Flood Prediction and Adaptive Farming Solutions Using IoT, Machine Learning, and Remote Sensing for Climate-Resilient Agriculture
source_title: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent Control Computing and Communications Ic3 2025
title_norm: flood prediction and adaptive farming solutions using iot machine learning and remote sensing for climateresilient agriculture
abstract: Flood is one of the most disastrous natural disasters to the people of agriculture, people and infrastructure. Mitigation of these risks and promotion of climate resilient agriculture depends on accurate flood predictions and progressive farming strategies. This paper presents an integrated model consisting of Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, Machine Learning (ML) and Remote Sensing technologies to provide precise, real time flood prediction and adaptive farming options. Using advanced deep learning algorithms and real time sensor data to predict and risk assess floods in real time, the model leverages real time satellite based Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR). Another function of the model is to offer adaptive farming solutions including optimized irrigation, flood resilient crop selection, and disaster recovery recommendations for regions impacted by the disaster. A hybrid AI technique assimilating the social media data, and blockchain for integrity of data is more effective to make decisions for the local authorities and farmers. This study seeks to fill the gaps in interdisciplinary collaboration, data scarcity and governance and provide a solution for flood management and sustainable agriculture as a whole.

title: Intelligent Sensor Based Smart Irrigation System For Sustainable Agriculture
source_title: 2024 International Conference on Communication Computing and Internet of Things Ic3iot 2024 Proceedings
title_norm: intelligent sensor based smart irrigation system for sustainable agriculture
abstract: In nations where water is scarce, effective water management is crucial. Since a lot of water is used for agriculture, the effective utilization of water resource is the need of the hour and this also has an impact on the country’s economy. The potential ramifications of global warming prompt the development of water adaptation strategies to guarantee water supply for food production and consumption. As a result, research on reducing the amount of water used for irrigation has grown over time. The Internet of Things (IoT) is not only essential to industry 4.0, but it can also be used in smart farming. The work being presented here aims to create an intelligent, low-cost watering system. Here, water is supplied to the crop depending on the moisture content of the soil as well as the time period for sowing, growing and harvesting of crops. The moisture content of the soil is detected by using the moisture sensor and the collected data is forwarded to the Arduino, which acts as the processor deciding the opening and closing of solenoid valves to maintain the prescribed soil moisture level (dependent on the type of crop). The solenoid valve will be opened when moisture level falls below the threshold level. The solenoid valve can be programmed to perform automated tasks namely changing the direction, flow and speed of the water. The solenoid valve will be closed once the water level is attained. The advantages of the proposed system are limited manual intervention, efficient utilization of water resources, reduced electricity requirement with economically feasible hardware components.
