title: Smart Irrigation Optimization with IoT and Weather Forecasts for Sustainable Crop Management
source_title: Proceedings IEEE 2024 1st International Conference on Advances in Computing Communication and Networking Icac2n 2024
title_norm: smart irrigation optimization with iot and weather forecasts for sustainable crop management
abstract: Proper water management is crucial in agriculture, especially for crops like paddy, corn, chili, and cotton. Uncertain weather conditions and inconsistent irrigation practices can result in either excessive water use or inadequate irrigation, both of which harm crop yields. Traditional irrigation methods typically rely on current weather conditions and even though they consider future weather, they fail to specify precise watering parameters like watering time. These methods are often for small scale and generalized, lacking the necessary specificity for different crops, which require varying watering durations. Consequently, they lack the precision needed for optimal water utilization, leading to water wastage and reduced yields. This project proposes an IoT-based smart irrigation system that uses weather prediction data collected from the web to provide accurate watering schedules. The system employs NodeMCU ESP8266 modules and soil moisture sensors, utilizing machine learning algorithms to analyze the weather data, monitor soil moisture, and forecast rainfall. By combining real-time soil moisture data with rainfall predictions, the system calculates optimal watering durations to ensure efficient water use. After displaying the recommended watering duration to the user, the system activates the irrigation motor for the specified amount of time upon user approval. This smart irrigation technology significantly improves water management and crop yields by automatically adjusting irrigation based on real environmental conditions, minimizing water wastage, and promoting sustainable farming.

title: Exploring Advanced Smart Sensing Technology for Enhanced Drip Irrigation Management in Greenhouses
source_title: 2024 International Conference on Advances in Computing Communication Electrical and Smart Systems Innovation for Sustainability Icaccess 2024
title_norm: exploring advanced smart sensing technology for enhanced drip irrigation management in greenhouses
abstract: Drip irrigation systems have become an integral part of modern greenhouse farming practices as they help irrigate plants effectively and also supply plants with water and nutrients in precise amounts. Nevertheless, these technologies have to be perfectly adjusted to efficiently utilize water and boost crop yield. This research addresses two issues: firstly, the capacity of the sensing technology innovations for greenhouse drip irrigation to be more efficient, and secondly, sustainability. The study looked for several types of sensors and materials that can be used in the construction of the system section that take into consideration the information from the intelligent sensors and the monitoring of environmental parameters. The methodology used in the study was a methodological review. This paper will discuss the literature dealing with different mechanisms, tools, and materials to control environmental factors that could affect the drip irrigation system in greenhouses. The literature review presented several types of sensors, including temperature sensors, soil moisture sensors, and humidity sensors, which are the key components for intelligent greenhouse drip irrigation systems operating correctly. Embedding these sensors and materials in a comprehensive system has exhibited a positive effect on water consumption reduction and nutrient uptake by plants. The results of the discussion stress the high sensitivity to the choice of materials and sensors which consequence can be the deployment of the system for a long time and its high performance. Looking at the results, it is accordingly determined after the fact that sensor type and sensor materials constitute an essential part that would aid in achieving the best results with smart greenhouses through drip irrigation systems. These technologies ensure precise environmental monitoring and resource management, offering a pathway to sustainable and high-yield agriculture. The findings collected from this literature review can greatly push forward the latest demands for smart farming in the future.

title: A Smart Irrigation System Powered by IoT and Machine Learning for Optimal Water Management
source_title: 2024 4th International Conference on Advance Computing and Innovative Technologies in Engineering Icacite 2024
title_norm: a smart irrigation system powered by iot and machine learning for optimal water management
abstract: In this innovative quest for more efficient irrigation, we investigate the combined use of sensor technology and machine intelligence to optimise agricultural water usage. We collect precise data on essential variables, including water flow, temperature, humidity, soil moisture, and water level, every 15 days by promptly deploying sensors in the field to monitor them in real-time. We use the vast amount of data available to us to train machine learning models, including Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), specifically for streams that are anticipated to have a certain distribution. CNN has exceptional precision with a decoding accuracy of 94.5% in visual signal interpretation, surpassing ANN, KNN, and RNN which achieve lower accuracies of 91.1%, 88.7%, and 83.6% respectively. Our investigation uncovers a fluid interaction between sensor data and model training, leading to each model exhibiting unique characteristics. These findings not only showease the accuracy with which machine learning can distribute water, but they also signify a noteworthy progress in resource-efficient and sustainable agriculture. In addition to generating mathematical discoveries, our research establishes the foundation for advanced irrigation systems that smoothly integrate mechanical and natural processes in agricultural fields.

title: Sensor-Driven Smart Irrigation System for Water Management
source_title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Applied Electronics and Engineering Icaee 2025
title_norm: sensordriven smart irrigation system for water management
abstract: Efficient and sustainable water management is essential for modern agriculture to mitigate challenges related to water scarcity and energy consumption. This paper presents a solar-powered Automatic Irrigation System designed to optimize water usage while minimizing reliance on conventional energy sources. The system integrates a capacitive soil moisture sensor and an ultrasonic distance sensor to automate irrigation control and monitor water levels in the storage tank. During testing, the system activated the water pump and green LED when the soil moisture reading exceeded 200, indicating adequate soil hydration. When the moisture level fell below 200, the pump was deactivated and a red LED was triggered, effectively preventing overwatering. Similarly, the ultrasonic sensor continuously monitored the tank water level, activating a red LED when the distance was less than 10 cm to indicate low water level, and a green LED when above 10 cm, ensuring timely refilling. The system operates entirely on solar energy, eliminating the need for grid power and making it suitable for remote or off-grid agricultural areas. Observations confirm the system's reliability in automating irrigation based on real-time sensor inputs. This intelligent, energy-efficient, and scalable solution supports precision farming, promotes water conservation, and advances sustainable agricultural practices.

title: Stress Analysis of 'Ashwagandha, a Medicinal Plant' Using Thermal Imaging
source_title: 2025 1st International Conference on Aiml Applications for Engineering and Technology Icaet 2025
title_norm: stress analysis of ashwagandha a medicinal plant using thermal imaging
abstract: Plant stress is a significant challenge that affects plant growth, yield, and medicinal properties. Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera), a highly valued medicinal plant, is especially prone to water stress, making early detection of this stress essential for healthy development. Thermal imaging, a technology that measures temperature variations on plant surfaces, has become an effective, non-invasive method for identifying stress in plants without causing harm. This review explores existing studies on the application of thermal imaging to monitor water stress in ashwagandha. It explains how shifts in temperature can signal stress due to water shortages and how early identification can lead to more accurate water management practices. The review also highlights areas requiring further exploration and discusses the potential of combining thermal imaging with machine learning and other technological advancements to improve precision agriculture. Through the use of thermal imaging, this approach holds promise for promoting healthier crops, enhancing water efficiency, and supporting sustainable farming practices, especially in regions facing water shortages.

title_norm: green guardian iot driven water management for sustainable agriculture
abstract: Water scarcity is the most persistent problem on earth, especially in agriculture, due to inefficiency in its usage which reflects on the health and productivity of crops. This paper aims to propose a Smart Irrigation System that could save water better and consume resources much better. The system includes capacitive moisture soil sensors; temperature and humidity sensors with IoT-based protocol communication that relays conditions live. The methodology uses machine learning algorithms to generate predictions over time for the water requirement of different species of plants according to their seasonal behaviours. This led the tests to decline water intakes between 30 and 40, thus furthering the view of a sustainable agriculture way of life. This system has an intercommunication interface with the smartphone, meaning it can be set from afar and its scheduling changed with minimal on-site manual monitoring. This technology can easily scale up to work on a range of crops and climatic conditions, hence highly applicable in agriculture. It also does not interfere with already laid sprinkler and drip irrigation systems as such; hence it is easy to adapt the already existing infrastructure. Further studies will be on AI-based models of weather forecasting that will even improve their level of accuracy. Intelligent irrigation systems help to save water through proper health and increased productivity in agriculture because this corrects many and severe problems in the agricultural sector.

title: Application of remote sensing techniques for water resources planning and management
source_title: 2006 International Conference on Advances in Space Technologies Icast
title_norm: application of remote sensing techniques for water resources planning and management
abstract: This paper describes the importance and capabilities of modern techniques such as remote sensing (RS) and geographic information systems (GIS) as water resource management and conservation tool. RS/GIS analysis can show where water enters a system and how it leaves through evapotranspiration and runoff. Using this information, planners can identify areas where there is potential for development of new water resources; where water can be reallocated from one use or one basin to another; and identify potential areas of water scarcity before water shortages occur. The main objective of this research is to calculate accurate crop water requirement by using RS/GIS in combination with hydraulic models. The results helped in devising guidelines, which in turn will help the policy makers to release the water supplies based on crop requirement only rather than supply based. Multi temporal satellite images were used to identify various crops and cropping pattern in the area. This study was conducted for the Pehure high level canal (PHLC) and the upper Swat canal (USC) system in the North Western Frontier Province (NWFP) of Pakistan. Crop identification at distributary level was made from multi-temporal remote sensing satellite images. Various image processing techniques such as supervised, unsupervised classification and spectral mixture analysis were used to correctly identify various types of crops in the region and ultimately accurate areas of all the classified crops was calculated from the satellite images. These calculated areas were compared with the seasonal data recorded by the irrigation department. ET was calculated using CROPWAT model at various stages of crop growth. Then water required for each individual crop was calculated. The results are very encouraging. The results of this study can be used while devising guidelines for water managers to release the canal supplies based on crop water requirement This practice will help in avoiding wastage of canal water at farm level, which can be optimally used for increasing irrigated areas and crop productivity in the area.

title: Smart Irrigation Prediction Using Machine Learning
source_title: 2025 International Conference on Business Intelligence for Technology Innovation Icbiti 2025
title_norm: smart irrigation prediction using machine learning
abstract: Effective water management in agriculture is imperative for the sustainable and judicious utilization of resources, particularly in areas grappling with the scarcity of water. Conventional irrigation techniques that are inclined towards over-irrigating or under-irrigating can terribly degrade crop productivity and proper resource-saving. This paper investigates a new AI outlook to produce a smart irrigation forecasting program that optimizes water consumption based on real-time environmental data. In this project, the program is put to the test using combinations of weather conditions such as soil moisture zone, temperature, and humidity, the model predicts the best irrigation plan for various crop types. The prediction accuracy is improved by using a combination of supervised learning methods, and the model is trained on open datasets so that it can be scaled and customized to different crops and farming techniques. The results of the evaluation demonstrate the efficiency of the model, where water usage could be cut down by as much as 30% when compared to normal irrigation methods. This study provides the foundation for the deployment of smart irrigation systems that can be incorporated within farming practices, enhance responsible water management, and improve agricultural output.

title: Energy Consumption Forecasting in Smart Agriculture
source_title: 2025 International Conference on Business Intelligence for Technology Innovation Icbiti 2025
title_norm: energy consumption forecasting in smart agriculture
abstract: In the process of modernization of agriculture, in smart agriculture, optimizing energy consumption has become a crucial prerequisite for the sustainable operations of agriculture and reduction of the costs. In this study, we aim to enhance the robotics and energy efficiency, by developing a smart agricultural energy forecasting model based on real-time data and advanced machine learning techniques. Our approach integrates the analysis of energy requirements for various farming activities such as irrigation, greenhouse climate control, and automated machinery with the creation of predictive insights to enable efficient energy allocation. The energy forecasting model that we propose combines the historical data about energy consumption with environmental factors such as the weather and the crop growth phases to predict a more accurate answer. Such an approach can support the implementation of a federated learning framework that protects the data privacy of multiple farms while also improving the model on the whole. The outcomes of the application of the model indicate that the model could provide an energy service forecasting with very high accuracy, which in turn enabled farmers to take proactive measures to their energy consumption and subsequently resulted in the optimization of resource management together with the assistance of transition to usage of greener farming practices. This research can be identified as a valuable addition to the flourishing field of smart agriculture since it produces a scalable, privacy-preserving energy management solution.

abstract: Smart irrigation systems have been identified as a fundamental answer to the pressing requirement for effective water management in agriculture. This research investigates the usage of a variety of machine learning techniques for the purpose of optimizing irrigation control, aiming at a more improved water-use efficiency and simultaneously a healthy crop yield. title: AI for Optimizing Water Usage in Agriculture
source_title: 2025 International Conference on Business Intelligence for Technology Innovation Icbiti 2025
title_norm: ai for optimizing water usage in agriculture
abstract: Water efficiency is essential for the sustainability of agriculture, particularly in places where climate change and population growth cause water shortages. The purpose of this paper is to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) is used to reduce water consumption in agriculture. By using AI models with IoT sensors and precision irrigation systems that permeate the fields, the data with real-time parameters associated with the moisture content of the soil, the daily weather forecast, the water demands of the crops can be analyzed, and the right amount of water is the solution. A discussion covers such tools as machine learning for predictive analysis, deep learning for pattern recognition, and reinforcement learning for adaptive irrigation strategies. The research discusses the ways in which these AI technologies can decrease water loss, maximize crop yield, and minimize costs. Through case studies and experimental results, the ability of AI to transform water management in agriculture is presented, making it possible for more sustainable and efficient farming practices.

title: A Multifunctional UAV System for Precision Agriculture and Environmental Monitoring
source_title: 2025 2nd International Conference on New Frontiers in Communication Automation Management and Security Iccams 2025
title_norm: a multifunctional uav system for precision agriculture and environmental monitoring
abstract: Today, precision agriculture as a modern approach to farming has been aided by advanced technology for optimizing crop management and resource utilization. A multifunctional UAV system for real-time environmental monitoring in agriculture landscapes is presented here. This drone has a Pixhawk flight controller and a variety of environmental sensors from which air quality using the MQ-135, soil moisture, temperature using DHT22, water pollution, and LIDAR-based distance sensors (VL53L0X) would be applied. Moreover, it has an SD card-associated black box for safe data storage, allows solar charging so it can have a much longer mission time, and permits autonomous water landing when necessary for better survivability in emergency situations. The UAV can provide accurate environmental data which could help farmers or environmental agencies in decision making with regards to irrigation, fertilization, or pollution control. The efficiency of capturing accurate sensors data is verified through test results that also show the solar charging-enabled extended mission endurance and miss emergency landings without damage to critical components. The cashless data integrity is ensured with the black box mechanism. The system is also far superior to conventional systems based on ground monitoring in terms of scalability, flexibility, and reduced cost. In the future, research initiatives will focus on developing machine learning algorithms that enable improved navigation and decision-making in a more autonomous fashion, with the real-time capability for dynamic field management. This UAV-based precision agriculture platform thus assures sustainable agriculture by reducing wastages, improving productivity, and preventing environmental degradation.

title: Federated Learning-Based IoT in Smart Agriculture: Trends, Challenges, and Future Prospects
source_title: 2025 IEEE 7th International Conference on Computing Communication and Automation Iccca 2025
title_norm: federated learningbased iot in smart agriculture trends challenges and future prospects
abstract: Smart agriculture reduces costs and associated negative environmental effects while increasing productivity, sustainability, and efficiency through the use of technologies like DL, ML, IoT, and cloud computing. These technologies assist farmers in optimizing resources such as insecticides, fertilizer, water, and fuel. by gathering and analyzing decentralized data from sensors, drones, and satellite photos. This data-driven approach automates processes like irrigation, pest control, and fertilization, reducing labor and waste. However, the distributed nature of agricultural data raises privacy and security concerns. Traditional centralized ML methods require sharing sensitive data, which poses risks. Federated learning solves this by allowing data to stay local while models are trained and aggregated centrally. FL ensures data privacy, enables collaboration, and improves model performance, making it ideal for agriculture. By supporting localized training, FL enhances fuel efficiency, cuts costs, and reduces environmental impact. Together, smart agriculture and federated learning promote sustainable, efficient farming practices while safeguarding data privacy.

A smart solution can be a smart irrigation system that takes into account the water requirements, soil moisture levels, ambient environmental conditions, air moisture level and optimizes the water usage with minimal human intervention.

title: Distributed data reduction with decision-making for IoT-based smart farming irrigation systems
source_title: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies Icccnt 2023
title_norm: distributed data reduction with decisionmaking for iotbased smart farming irrigation systems
abstract: The more crucial process and one of the world's major consumers of water in agriculture is irrigation, which has been growing as a result of population growth and the resulting rise in demand for food. The irrigation system is one of the most important components of a system of agriculture. The crop's productivity will be directly influenced by the efficiency and applicability of the irrigation system. Water scarcity is one of the greatest challenges for an irrigation system. The efficient use of land, water, and energy resources depends on Internet of Things (IoT)-based smart agriculture systems. In this article, a distributed data reduction and decision-making (DiDaReD) approach for IoT-based smart farming irrigation systems is proposed. The DiDaReD approach is implemented on two levels: sensor devices and edge gateway. At the sensor device level, we implemented a lightweight scoring method for removing the redundant collected soil moisture readings before sending them to the edge gateway. At the edge of the gateway, a voting technique is applied to the scores of received readings from sensor devices to produce a decision regarding irrigation of the monitored farming field according to the soil moisture state of this field. Finally, since the DiDaReD approach is periodic and works in real-time, we implement a decision reduction algorithm to prevent sending the same decision notifications to the actuator, thus saving the energy of the IoT network. Several experiments are implemented using real sensed data from the farming field, and the conducted results show that the proposed DiDaReD outperforms other methods in terms of data reduction ratio, number of sent readings, energy consumption, network lifetime, data integrity, decisions, and total energy consumed by the edge-gateway node.

title: 'Smart Irrigation System by Detecting Plant Squeals Using IoT'
source_title: 2025 International Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies Iccct 2025
title_norm: smart irrigation system by detecting plant squeals using iot
abstract: Water scarcity is an escalating global issue driven by population growth and increasing demands from agriculture, industry, and domestic use. Effective water management is essential for achieving sustainable development. This paper introduces a Smart Irrigation System that combines Internet of Things (IoT) technologies with insights from plant physiology to optimize water efficiency. The system employs sensors to monitor environmental factors such as soil moisture, temperature, and humidity, as well as ultrasonic sounds produced by stressed plants. A Raspberry Pi Pico microcontroller analyzes this data, and the setup is connected to ThingSpeak and MATLAB for real-time data evaluation and monitoring. By linking plant distress signals to environmental conditions, the system facilitates precision irrigation, reducing water wastage while improving plant health. The proposed approach is scalable and adaptable for both small-scale and commercial agricultural uses. Future enhancements will focus on machine learning models for predictive analytics, improved signal filtering techniques, and the integration of renewable energy to further boost system efficiency and sustainability.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Precision Irrigation for Ideal Water Use in Arid Areas
source_title: 2025 International Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies Iccct 2025
title_norm: deep reinforcement learningbased precision irrigation for ideal water use in arid areas
abstract: Sustainable food production depends on agriculture using water efficiently, especially in arid areas. A revolutionary method for optimizing water distribution based on current environmental circumstances and crop needs is precision irrigation, which makes use of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). This study introduces a unique framework for dynamically monitoring and controlling irrigation systems by combining sophisticated DRL algorithms with Internet of Things-enabled sensors. The suggested approach provides accurate irrigation schedules that adjust to changing conditions by taking into account crop-specific water demands, soil moisture levels, and weather forecasts. Our strategy maximizes agricultural productivity while placing a high priority on resource efficiency. In contrast to conventional irrigation techniques, which frequently lead to water waste and less-than-ideal crop health, the DRL-based system continuously learns and enhances its decision-making process, guaranteeing the best possible water application in a variety of situations. Extensive tests were carried out on controlled agricultural conditions and real-world datasets to validate the framework, showing a notable 25% decrease in water consumption when compared to conventional methods. title: Development of Intelligent Irrigation System in Rice Field using Low-power Control Equipment
source_title: 2023 International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Complex Data Iccd 2023
title_norm: development of intelligent irrigation system in rice field using lowpower control equipment
abstract: Rice cultivation, a staple crop that sustains billions of people globally, faces significant challenges in terms of water management, labor efficiency, and productivity. China, as the largest producer and consumer of rice, predominantly relies on traditional flood irrigation via open canals, which is both labor-intensive and results in substantial water wastage. To address these challenges, this research presents the development and implementation of an intelligent irrigation system tailored to open canal rice cultivation. This intelligent irrigation system leverages automation and remote monitoring to enhance convenience, productivity, and safety, especially for the aging farming demographic. The system's core components include intelligent water lifting stations, gate transformations, wireless irrigation control, and an intelligent irrigation management platform. By seamlessly integrating these elements, the system optimizes water distribution, reduces labor requirements, and enhances crop yields. The research contributes to the modernization and digitization of rice cultivation practices, emphasizing water resource conservation and addressing agricultural sector challenges. Through multi-site trials, the system's capabilities are demonstrated to significantly reduce water consumption in rice paddies while maintaining crop yields. Water savings range from 2.9% to 19.3%, depending on seasonal conditions. Furthermore, the system's remote monitoring and control features reduce labor needs by approximately 35-40%, offering convenience and productivity benefits. This work highlights the potential of intelligent irrigation to improve the sustainability of rice farming, providing a pathway towards efficient water application, labor savings, and increased crop productivity.

It represents a step forward in promoting sustainable farming practices by reducing water consumption and improving agricultural productivity.

title: Bi-LSTM and ARIMA Approach for Soil-Specific Water Requirement Analysis
source_title: Proceedings of the 2025 International Conference on Computational Innovations and Sustainable Technologies Iccist 2025
title_norm: bilstm and arima approach for soilspecific water requirement analysis
abstract: Efficient water management is essential for sustainable agriculture, particularly in the face of climate change and limited water resources. This project presents a comprehensive approach for analyzing soilspecific water requirements using advanced predictive models, namely Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) and Auto Regressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA). By integrating these models, we aim to achieve high accuracy in predicting water requirements for various crops based on soil properties, crop types, and climatic factors. The Bi-LSTM model is designed to capture sequential dependencies in the dataset, while ARIMA is applied for robust time series forecasting. In the PINN approach, the LSTM-based sequence-to-sequence and feedforward neural network models were trained using a cost function incorporating the hydrological model and observed data. Our simulations showed that the two investigated frameworks improved predictions compared to purely using data-driven or the hydrological model, demonstrating the potential of hybrid machine learning frameworks for accurately modeling soil moisture dynamics for guiding agricultural and hydrological applications.Knowledge of the soil water retention (SWR) data is necessary for modeling soil water movement and assessing soil water holding capacity and availability. Since direct measurement is often time-consuming and costly, pretransfer functions (PTFs) have been widely used to predict SWR data from basic soil physical properties. Natural logarithm of soil suction, In (h), is considered as an extra input parameter in this approach. It enables us to predict SWR data at any desired soil suction as it results in more extensive and useful database. To train and validate this model, a real-world dataset containing a set of parameters related to weather forecasting, soil moisture, and other related parameters was collected using smart sensors installed in a greenhouse in Chiang Mai province, Thailand. Preliminary results show that our LSTM-based model performs well in predicting soil moisture with a $0.72 \%$ RMSE error and a $0.52 \%$ cross- validation error (LSTM), and our Bi-LSTM model with a $0.76 \%$ RMSE error and a $0.57 \%$ cross- validation error. In the future, we aim to test and validate this model on other similar datasets. Finally, the proposed Bi-LSTM and ARIMA hybrid model provides a powerful tool for soil-specific water requirement forecasting. It bridges the gap between statistical accuracy and deep learning flexibility, offering a promising direction for smart irrigation systems and data- driven agricultural water management in the era of climate uncertainty.

title: Design and Development of Solar Powered IoT Enabled Multi-layer Soil Moisture Probe
source_title: 2024 27th International Conference on Computer and Information Technology Iccit 2024 Proceedings
title_norm: design and development of solar powered iot enabled multilayer soil moisture probe
abstract: Technological development has been taking place at an expeditious pace over the last few decades, effecting our every aspect of life. However, the agricultural sector so far by and large remains underdeveloped. By incorporating the neoteric advancements in IoT and modern technologies, we can revolutionize this sector, making it more efficient, sustainable, and productive. This research focuses on the development of IoT based solar powered Soil Moisture (SM) monitoring system which is also can be considered as plants’ root zone (SM based) monitoring technology. Instead of traditional method of monitoring the moisture of ground level, this research adopts a new method that monitors the moisture level of the soil at 5 different levels. Measuring temperature and moisture in multiple layers and points of soil allows for a precise and accurate understanding of the water requirements of crop roots during their growth phase. Additionally, it can enhance the water utilization efficiency and provide fundamental data for studying the variability of soil water infiltration and implementing intelligent and accurate irrigation. The developed probe features 5 soil moisture sensors placed at different depth at 30-180 cm depth, along with 3 temperature sensors at 50-150 cm depth and ESP8266 module to implement IoT connectivity. The sensor readings are transmitted to smartphone through an app that indicates the soil moisture level as well the temperature at various depths of soil. Significantly, the entire system operates on solar power, underscoring the commitment to green energy and sustainable practices. Initial results obtained from local farmland indicates that the system is reliable, efficient and accurate.

title: Empowering Farmers with AI: Risk Mitigation Through Machine Learning in Smart Irrigation Systems
source_title: Proceedings of International Conference on Circuit Power and Computing Technologies Iccpct 2024
title_norm: empowering farmers with ai risk mitigation through machine learning in smart irrigation systems
abstract: The advent of IoT-enabled smart irrigation systems in the domain of precision agriculture has revolutionized farming practices, significantly enhancing crop yield and resource management. However, this technological transformation has exposed farmers to novel challenges, particularly in the realms of security, privacy, and risk management. This research investigates the vital utilization of machine learning (ML) for intrusion detection in the case of smart farming, particularly in utilizing IoT technology to enhance and automate irrigation processes is a hallmark of modern precision agriculture, with the aim of mitigating risks. Farmers today face an array of risks, from crop-specific threats such as pests and diseases to broader environmental factors like weather fluctuations. The effective prediction of these risks is essential for sustainable agriculture. Employing ML techniques, this research endeavors to develop an advanced intrusion detection system that not only safeguards smart irrigation infrastructure but also predicts and mitigates risks associated with crop health and water resource management. This holistic approach leverages data from various IoT sensors, including soil-moisture sensors, weather stations, and drone-based imagery, to provide immediate response into potential risks. While benefits in this technology are immense, it also brings security and privacy challenges, as the data generated and transmitted by these systems can be susceptible to unauthorized access and malicious manipulation. Our important aims are to equip farmers with an integrated solution that not only detects and prevents intrusions into their smart irrigation systems but also provides predictive insights into potential agricultural risks.

title: IoT-based Soil Nutrient Monitoring system with Smart Irrigation
source_title: International Conference on Computational Robotics Testing and Engineering Evaluation Iccrtee 2025
title_norm: iotbased soil nutrient monitoring system with smart irrigation
abstract: Agriculture forms the backbone of many economies, and its efficiency largely depends on effective soil and water management. This paper presents an IoT-based system for nutrient monitoring and smart irrigation. The system is equipped with sensors of NPK, pH, and soil moisture to measure various soil conditions in real-time. Sensor data is stored in a cloud platform such as ThinkSpeak with the assistance of IoT technology for analysis and visualization. The system irrigates automatically by activating a water pump when soil moisture is below 20% and deactivates irrigation when soil moisture increases up to 40%, to save water effectively. Additionally, fertilizer content is controlled based on NPK sensor values (N: 10-100 mg/kg, P: 5-50 mg/kg, K: 10-60 mg/kg) and pH levels (3-10), adjusting soil well-being for crop growth. It is estimated that it saves as much as 30% of water, reduces fertilizer loss by 25%, and boosts crop production by 15-20%, which is a cost-effective means for future agriculture.

title_norm: artificial intelligence and internet of things powered smart irrigation transforming agricultural efficiency and sustainability
abstract: Water is necessary for the establishment of empires and civilizations. Water has economic value because it supports agriculture, sustains rich ecosystems, and feeds people worldwide. It is impossible to estimate the terrible implications for the food supply chain and agriculture sector in the absence of water supplies. From a worldwide standpoint, a semiarid nation such as Morocco confronts two difficulties: climate change and water scarcity, which place significant strain on the region's food security as well as agricultural output. This challenge in water efficiency is addressed using cutting-edge technologies based on the Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI), allowing us to build a smart system for real-time monitoring and control of water usage in the fields. The system can monitor humidity, temperature, rainfall predictions, and tank water levels. The intelligent system under consideration determines whether to open the valve for soil irrigation or not. The system has several benefits in addition to optimizing water use. It also improves soil water retention by over-controlling flood irrigation and limiting unnecessary rainfall.

title: A sustainable agricultural system using IoT
source_title: Proceedings of the 2017 IEEE International Conference on Communication and Signal Processing Iccsp 2017
title_norm: a sustainable agricultural system using iot
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is an element of worldwide data that comprise of web associated items, or things implanted with gadgets, software, sensors and also different instruments which are becoming an integral component of future internet. This work developed a system which will automatically monitor the agricultural field as well as performing live video streaming for monitoring the Agriculture field from the server itself, through raspberry pi camera. The agriculture fields are monitored for environmental temperature, humidity and soil moisture. The automatic irrigation will be performed based on the set points of the temperature, humidity and soil moisture sensor. The data collected from the field are monitored in IoT, the data are then processed and necessary information is passed through the field owners for counter measures.

title: Mobile integrated smart irrigation management and monitoring system using IOT
source_title: Proceedings of the 2017 IEEE International Conference on Communication and Signal Processing Iccsp 2017
title_norm: mobile integrated smart irrigation management and monitoring system using iot
abstract: Agriculture has been the most important practice from very beginning of the human civilization. Traditional methods that are used for irrigation, such as overhead sprinkler and flood type, is not that much efficient. They results in a lot of wastage of water and can also promote disease such as fungus formation due to over moisture in the soil. Automated irrigation system is essential for conservation of the water and indirectly viability of the farm since it is an important commodity. About 85% of total available water resources across the world are solely used for the irrigation purpose. In upcoming years this demand is likely to increase because of increasing population. To meet this demand we must adopt new techniques which will conserve need of water for irrigation process. In automation system water availability to crop is monitored through sensors and as per need watering is done through the controlled irrigation. The almost infinite capabilities of storage and processing, the rapid elasticity makes cloud computing an attractive solution to the large amount of data generated. The idea is to focus on parameters such as temperature and soil moisture. This is a Mobile Integrated and smart irrigation system using IOT based on application controlled monitoring system. The main objective of this project is to control the water supply and monitor the plants through a Smartphone.

title: An IOT Based Agriculture Monitoring System
source_title: Proceedings of the 2018 IEEE International Conference on Communication and Signal Processing Iccsp 2018
title_norm: an iot based agriculture monitoring system
abstract: To meet the growing demand of irrigation in India due to uncertain climatic conditions it is necessary to focus on sustainable irrigation approaches and improving the efficiency of the existing irrigation systems. The main purpose of this paper is to analyze the soil moisture level and to afford with auto irrigation to the crops. This system also senses Humidity, temperature and to detect if there are any obstacles in the concerned area and to reduce the human intervention (farmers) for complete automation of the system. The proposed system consist f Raspberry Pi, various sensors, Pi camera and motor driver. In smart supervising system the pi camera captures the video and transfers it to cloud through Raspberry Pi. Here Pi camera is used to provide live video streaming. The soil moisture sensor detects the moisture level and irrigates the various crops in the controlled manner. If any variation in moisture level is sensed then the sensor will update the observed value to the microcontroller and store in the cloud. Depending upon the observed value the crops are automatically provided with water to the preferred level which maintains the humidity of the soil. The moisture level of the industrial area is detected using the Temperature and Humidity sensor and transfer it to cloud through Raspberry Pi. The PIR sensor senses the entry of obstacles in the restricted area and updates it to cloud. The user can obtain these data's from cloud via mobile. Based on these data's the user can control the operation of motor by passing the command YES/NO through motor driver. Here Raspberry pi interfaces with sensors, camera, motor driver and controls the entire system.

title: AgriSense: Advanced Environmental Monitoring for Crops
source_title: Proceedings of the 2024 10th International Conference on Communication and Signal Processing Iccsp 2024
title_norm: agrisense advanced environmental monitoring for crops
abstract: In addressing the challenges of irrigation in agriculture, the implementation of Internet of Things (IoT) technology emerges as a promising solution. The growing need for effective water management has put farmers at a disadvantage in optimizing irrigation systems to suit crop requirements while preserving resources. A smart IoT-based irrigation system that provides an effective solution to overcome these problems. By incorporating various sensors like humidity and moisture sensors with Arduino Mega, the system continuously monitors soil conditions and crop needs in real-time. Data collected from these sensors is transmitted to the cloud via IoT connectivity for analysis and storage. A user-friendly mobile application provides remote access to this data, offering insights into soil moisture levels, environmental factors, and irrigation schedules. Moreover, the app allows manual control of the irrigation system, enabling users to remotely toggle the pump on/off as required. Crucially, the microcontroller powering the system is solar-powered, enhancing sustainability and reducing dependence on external power sources. Combining IoT technology, Arduino Mega microcontrollers, and solar energy, this system represents a scalable and environmentally conscious approach to smart irrigation, addressing the pressing need for sustainable water management in agriculture.

title: CNN-LSTM Model for Cotton Yield Prediction Using Remote Sensing Data
source_title: 2025 6th International Conference on Data Intelligence and Cognitive Informatics Icdici 2025
title_norm: cnnlstm model for cotton yield prediction using remote sensing data
abstract: This research presents a hybrid CNN-LSTM model for predicting cotton production using remote sensing data. The model integrates the spatial feature extraction capability of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with the temporal sequence modeling proficiency of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. Remote sensing data, including satellite and aerial images, are analyzed by CNN to extract essential spatial information about vegetation health, land use, and crop conditions. The characteristics are then input into the LSTM network, which examines temporal fluctuations and environmental factors to forecast cotton production over time. The proposed model was evaluated using a dataset comprising remote sensing images collected over multiple growth seasons. The findings indicate that the model's performance in forecasting cotton production is 98.6% accurate. The increased accuracy indicates that the CNN-LSTM model effectively captures spatial and temporal changes, making it a formidable instrument for precision agriculture. The model's capacity to precisely predict cotton production may enhance resource management, optimize irrigation, and promote sustainable agricultural practices, augmenting agricultural productivity.

title: HydroSavvy: Modernizing Agriculture with Intelligent Irrigation Solutions Using IoT
source_title: 2025 International Conference on Data Science Agents and Artificial Intelligence Icdsaai 2025
title_norm: hydrosavvy modernizing agriculture with intelligent irrigation solutions using iot
abstract: This research introduces a new term, Hydro-Savvy. It is an innovative, intelligent irrigation system that optimizes water application and increases crop yields using the Internet of Things, Artificial Intelligence, and advanced sensors. Among the features include the mesh network of soil moisture sensors to obtain real-time data on scheduling irrigation, flow meters that offer insight into water usage, and leak detection to monitor the pump and valves in order not to waste water. It is accessible even where the internet might be small, and it uses solar panels with a battery backup to work 24/7. The multilingual AI mobile application supports voice commands and assists in real-time water consumption tracking, maintaining logs of irrigation activities, efficiency reports, and guidelines for saving water. The system integrates with the weather API, thus preventing drought irrigation, while machine learning models predict the likelihood of future irrigations as required based on data about weather, soil, and crops. The backend coding is Node.js, with data stored on Google Cloud and Firebase. This research exemplifies the potential for IoT and AI to revolutionize water management toward sustainability and better agricultural productivity.

title: IoT-Enabled Smart Irrigation Framework Leveraging Stacked Machine Learning Algorithms
source_title: 3rd IEEE International Conference on Data Science and Network Security Icdsns 2025
title_norm: iotenabled smart irrigation framework leveraging stacked machine learning algorithms
abstract: The growing need for sustainable agriculture requires innovative solutions that optimize water usage without compromising crop yield. This paper presents an Intelligent Irrigation Framework that leverages real-time sensor data from the Smart Farming Data 2024 dataset along with a robust ensemble model to enhance irrigation efficiency. The dataset includes environmental parameters such as soil moisture, ambient temperature, humidity levels, and precipitation, recorded through IoT-based sensing infrastructure. These realtime inputs are processed through a layered ensemble of machine learning models to deliver precise and reliable irrigation recommendations. Current systems lack sufficient flexibility, require high human intervention, and often rely on single-model forecasts, resulting in inefficient water management. Conventional models, such as threshold-based automation or simple regression, lack the adaptability to respond to changing field conditions. To address this concern, the proposed stack integrates Random Forest, Support Vector Regression (SVR), and LightGBM to form a hybrid prediction engine that combines the strengths of each model. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 99.2% and an F1-score of 98.1%. This highperformance approach demonstrates flexibility, accuracy, and reliability in delivering smart irrigation scheduling.

title: Recent advancements of Internet of Things in Precision Agriculture: A Review
source_title: 2023 International Conference on Disruptive Technologies Icdt 2023
title_norm: recent advancements of internet of things in precision agriculture a review
abstract: The requirement for producing food is rising as the world's population rises. The decline of the workforce in rural areas and the rise in production costs are other issues the food industry is currently dealing with. The Internet of Things (IoT) could be used in "smart farming," a concept in farm management that aims to address the current issues in food production. This emerging paradigm aims to connect various intelligent physical elements in order to modernise various domains. Numerous IoT-based frameworks have been developed to manage and track agricultural lands automatically and with the least amount of human involvement. Based on statistical and quantitative methods, the current agricultural system can be revolutionised more effectively. In a green field, one can also encounter irrigation, plant diseases, different crop stages, and drone activation from IoT. The discussion of how IoT uses sensors for a variety of purposes. The main objective of this research is to create cutting-edge IoT tools and concepts for modern agricultural practises. Systematic evaluation provides information on current and future trends in the agricultural sector..

title: AI-Enhanced Disease Identification and Yield Optimization in Seasonal Agriculture: A Comparative Analysis
source_title: Icdt 2025 3rd International Conference on Disruptive Technologies
title_norm: aienhanced disease identification and yield optimization in seasonal agriculture a comparative analysis
abstract: The agricultural industry is essential for global food security, economic stability, and employment, especially in developing countries. Crop diseases represent a substantial risk to productivity, with yearly yield reductions of 20-40%. Traditional illness detection techniques, dependent on eye examination, are frequently sluggish, labour-intensive, and susceptible to mistakes. This research examines the progress in agricultural disease identification, contrasting conventional methods with contemporary technology such as machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and remote sensing. Deep learning models, especially Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), have exhibited exceptional efficacy in disease detection, attaining accuracy rates of 90% in crops such as tomato, potato, and rice. The amalgamation of hyperspectral imaging, drone surveillance, and AI-powered instruments facilitates early illness identification, continuous monitoring, and scalable solutions. The transition to digital agriculture not only optimizes disease management but also increases crop output, facilitating sustainable agricultural techniques to address the rising global food demands.

title: Histogram-Based Analysis of UAV-SAR Data for Agricultural Vegetation Classification
source_title: Proceedings of the International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications Iceaa
title_norm: histogrambased analysis of uavsar data for agricultural vegetation classification
abstract: Climate change poses new challenges and efficiency requirements for the agricultural sector. This necessitates the coordination of fertilization and irrigation efforts by monitoring crop. Precision agriculture aims to achieve this using modern technology including unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). This paper shows a histogram-based approach to distinguish between crops by evaluating data of a high-performance UAV-based dual band radar at 1-4 GHz and 6-9 GHz. Three agricultural fields, were selected for this study, one each for maize, barley, and wheat. High-resolution synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images are generated for each crop in order to differentiate them based on amplitude distributions, as well as elevation dependencies.

title_norm: iotdriven smart irrigation for paddy cultivation using bcoresnet a deep learning approach
abstract: Raising crop yield and simultaneously addressing the worldwide water shortage issue depends on good water management in paddy farming. Considered conventional irrigation methods often waste water, cause poor monitoring, and produce insufficient crops. title: A Review on the Use of Smart Agriculture Systems to Protect Crops
source_title: 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Renewable Systems Icears 2025 Proceedings
title_norm: a review on the use of smart agriculture systems to protect crops
abstract: Smart agriculture systems leverage the possibilities offered by cutting-edge technologies such as IoT, AI, and remote sensing to revolutionize conventional farming by enhancing resource utilization, production, and crop damage mitigation. Real-time monitoring of soil and crop health, predictive analytics, pest control, and precision irrigation measures are all enabled by these systems. They are able to address major Indian agriculture issues, consequently boosting yield and profitability and promoting environmental sustainability. The largescale deployment of intelligent agriculture systems will change the agriculture landscape in India and will assure long-term food security for an ever-growing population. Challenges include adequate research and future studies in order to better install and achieve smart agricultural systems to protect crops. Intelligent agriculture involves all advanced research, including science and innovations, in national development through space technologies to enhance soil quality, conserve water, and facilitate agriculture information. Space ventures will undergo improved modernization through the introduction of crop sprayers, precision gene editors, epigenetics, big data analytics, IoT, wind and photovoltaic smart energy, AI-enabled robotic applications, and wide-scale desalination technologies. Implementing digital farming systems in developing economies will help their sectors as 85 percent of the global population is set to live in developing countries by 2030. Automation will prove to be necessary since food scarcity is on the rise along with resource wastage. Control strategies such as the IoT, aerial imagery, machine learning, and artificial intelligence will boost production and prevent soil degradation. These advanced technologies are also able to alleviate such issues as plant disease detection, pesticide management, and water application. The introduction of the Internet of Things in the agricultural research world has started with an urge for such communication technologies to communicate and connect devices. The overall assessment of these technologies is, however, vague. This study, therefore, critically analyses 94 papers published on the IoT communication technologies in smart agriculture to highlight the challenges, suggest resolutions, and set recommendations for their application. The need to integrate technology with research was underscored.

title: A Smart Irrigation System for Coconut Farming using IoT
source_title: 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Renewable Systems Icears 2025 Proceedings
title_norm: a smart irrigation system for coconut farming using iot
abstract: Coconut farming is an essential agricultural practice that contributes significantly to the global economy by providing valuable products such as coconut water, oil, and meat. However, the management of coconut plantations faces numerous challenges, including labor shortages, pest control, and the demand for precise irrigation and fertilization. This paper proposes an integrated smart farming system that leverages advanced sensor technologies and automation to address these challenges. The system employs precision irrigation and fertigation methods, facilitated by a centralized motor controller and solenoid valves, to deliver water and nutrients efficiently to the base of each coconut tree. A pH sensor monitors soil acidity or alkalinity, ensuring optimal nutrient availability and promoting sustainable farming practices by reducing chemical inputs. Additional features include a tree motion sensor and a tilt sensor for monitoring tree stability under adverse weather conditions. Soil moisture sensors, temperature, humidity, and light intensity sensors provide real-time data to enhance decision-making. Farmers can remotely monitor and control the system via a Node-RED dashboard, receiving alerts through platforms like Telegram. By integrating these technologies, the proposed system aims to optimize resource utilization, enhance crop yield, and reduce the environmental impact of coconut farming.

title: Cloud based automated irrigation and plant leaf disease detection system using an android application
source_title: Proceedings of the International Conference on Electronics Communication and Aerospace Technology Iceca 2017
title_norm: cloud based automated irrigation and plant leaf disease detection system using an android application
abstract: Due to drastic climatic changes and scarcity of water, the need for proper and sustainable irrigation methods is of high demand. The water demand for plants varies from place to place with the changes in soil content, texture, climatic factors and so on. The plants need to be irrigated according to their water requirements at that climatic conditions. As like as the water requirements, plant diseases are also a factor that keeps the plants not growing properly. Also, a variety of plant leaf diseases have also been detected nowadays. In this paper, a novel smart irrigation system has been proposed which can control the irrigation automatically using an android mobile application. Apart from this, the photos of plant leaves are captured and are sent to the cloud server, which is further processed and compared with the diseased plant leaf images in the cloud database. Based on the comparison a list of plant diseases suspected are given to the user via the android mobile application.

title: Arduino based Automation of Agriculture A Step towards Modernization of Agriculture
source_title: Proceedings of the 4th International Conference on Electronics Communication and Aerospace Technology Iceca 2020
title_norm: arduino based automation of agriculture a step towards modernization of agriculture
abstract: Agriculture in the modern age is changing rapidly. The increasing global population and shifting trade policies affect the pricing, supply chain, and delivery of food products. Meanwhile, consumer preferences, especially in western countries are shifting toward organic food and sustainably-produced vegetables and fruits that require more labour. There are about 53% population of India is engaged in agricultural activities. The growing and changing demands that need to be met by an agriculture industry are now facing labour shortages and rising costs for farm work. The abovementioned problems can be solved by bringing automation in agriculture and thus modernization of agriculture came into the picture. In this work, the most primal goal of reducing the required man labour is achieved by bringing automation in various phases involved in the cultivation of crops. To achieve actions like ploughing, planting, and cutting, an automated vehicle is designed and controlled. Smart sensors and advanced communication technologies are used to achieve remote control of the vehicle. To reduce the amount of water wasted, an irrigation system is designed which waters the field based on the weather forecast and moisture in the soil. To achieve this, a mechanism is designed which predicts the weather and selects the crop for the particular season. A prototype is developed in this paper for ploughing. The vehicle is steered in all the possible direction using H-bridge driven DC motor. The motor is controlled using a mobile app and Blue-tooth communication between the farmer and the vehicle which will be in the field and thus achieving remote control. In this paper automation of vehicle for ploughing and planting is presented.

source_title: 7th International Conference on Electronics Communication and Aerospace Technology Iceca 2023 Proceedings

abstract: Irrigation, fertilisation, and crop rotation has gained paramount importance in the agricultural industry. Technological advances motivate farmers to achieve optimum crop yields. Maximising crop yield via the deployment of cutting-edge agricultural technology is the recent research trend. Increased yields can be achieved by considering various parameters including soil temperature, soil pH, and water availability. This research work proposes the an IoT-based Precision Agriculture system called “ACRIS: Agriculture Cultivation Recommender and Smart Irrigation System” to provide helpful suggestions to farmers interested in increasing the crop yields by using the Internet of Things technology. The suggested method works well in monitoring the agricultural crops. The proposed system is also capable of determining future irrigation planning requirements. Soil conditions like moisture, temperature, and humidity are used as predictors. These experimental results show that the smart irrigation may increase the crop output while decreasing water usage.

title: Automated Horticulture for Farmers Using IoT
source_title: Proceedings of the 2nd International Conference on Edge Computing and Applications Icecaa 2023
title_norm: automated horticulture for farmers using iot
abstract: India is a country that focuses on raising crops. The agricultural understanding was everything to our ancient populations. The majority of Indians depend on agriculture for their daily needs, and it has a significant impact on the nation's economy. Irrigation becomes challenging in dry areas or cases of little rainfall. To provide the best results and safeguard farmers, it must be forced upon them. A substantial role is played by horticulture, a subsector of agriculture, in the economy, human nutrition, gender mainstreaming, and employment. Fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices, and sauces are examples of horticultural goods, which have continuously increased and now make up a significant portion of the agricultural trade. The purpose of the automatic irrigation control system is to decrease the efforts of the human operator (gardener) in horticulture operations. The goal of the horticulture system is to maintain measures of food security. Farmlands have historically had their soil moisture levels checked manually. This is frequently time-consuming and ineffective, thus a method that is effective at regulating and keeping track of soil moisture levels is required. To communicate data from the board to the user's smartphone or laptop, this study presents an Internet of Things (IoT)-based soil moisture monitor that uses ESP32 with an integrated Wi-Fi module to monitor soil moisture level. The soil moisture monitors measure the amount of water in the soil and notify the farmer when the moisture sensor's predetermined threshold rate rises or falls, indicating overwatering or underwatering, respectively. This control system is based on an Arduino that has been coded in embedded C. Data from the sensor is also transmitted during this procedure, first to the cloud and subsequently to the database server. By ensuring that water is not wasted, the proposed soil moisture monitor's evaluation utilizing ThingSpeak.

title: Revitalizing Lebanon's Energy Sector: A Hybrid Waste-to-Energy Solution in the Chouf District
source_title: International Conference on Electrical Computer Communications and Mechatronics Engineering Iceccme 2025
title_norm: revitalizing lebanons energy sector a hybrid wastetoenergy solution in the chouf district
abstract: The global energy sector is transforming due to technological advancements and renewable energy adoption. Conversely, Lebanon faces challenges such as outdated infrastructure, frequent power outages, and financial instability, with only 50% support for its electrical load. As the country enters the Fourth Industrial Revolution, it must modernize its energy network. This paper discusses the possibility of revitalizing the power sector through a hybrid waste-to-energy process, which can enhance electricity stability and handle municipality waste issues. The proposed hybrid approach uses three renewable energy technologies: anaerobic digester, gasification, and incineration. The theoretical equations of these three technologies are illustrated. A case study that takes the Chouf district of Lebanon is illustrated to prove the benefits of adopting this approach. The result shows that the integration of these three techniques succeeds in producing 104% of the required energy and also minimizes the waste volume and mass. Thus, the required space for final disposal becomes smaller. In addition, the anaerobic digester can produce water that forms a sustainable source for irrigation.

source_title: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical Computer and Communication Technologies Icecct 2023
title_norm: arithmetic optimization algorithm with machine learning based smart irrigation system in iot environment
abstract: An integration of new technologies like agro-hydroinformatics and computational intelligence, and information technology (IT) roles a vital play in developing a sustainable precision irrigation method with the effectual management of sensed data assuming plants, weather, and soil. Machine learning (ML) is a fast-developing technology for precision irrigation schemes, because of their capability to simulate human decision-making but also resolve the multi-variable, non-linear, and time-variant problems affecting irrigation management. An essential drive of ML is for providing data from preceding experiences and statistical data to machines towards it is carried out their allocated task of resolving a particular problem. Therefore, this study develops an Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm with Machine Learning based Smart irrigation system (AOAML-SIS) technique in IoT environment. Initially, the AOAML-SIS technique exploits the IoT sensors for data collection process. title: Renewable Energy Based Smart-Agriculture System
source_title: 3rd International Conference on Emerging Computation and Information Technologies Icecit 2025 Book of Abstracts
title_norm: renewable energy based smartagriculture system
abstract: Effective water management is essential to sustainable farming and efficient crop production in agriculture. A solar-powered smart irrigation monitoring system that maximises water utilisation, minimises manual labour, and increases crop productivity is presented in this research. The system uses an ESP-8266 microcontroller to integrate several sensors and automated components for real-time monitoring and control. The system has soil moisture sensors to measure the amount of water in the soil, temperature and humidity sensors to monitor the climate, and a rain sensor to prevent unnecessary watering when it rains. A motion sensor (PIR) increases security because it may detect undesired movement in the field. To ensure precise water distribution, a relay-controlled water pump is activated in response to sensor readings. By combining smart sensing technology with renewable energy, this project offers farmers a scalable and cost-effective solution that promotes sustainable agriculture practices.

title: Soil Moisture-Based Intelligent Irrigation System with IoT and Cloud Computing for Precision Agriculture and Water Conservation
source_title: Proceedings Iceconf 2025 2025 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Knowledge Discovery in Concurrent Engineering
title_norm: soil moisturebased intelligent irrigation system with iot and cloud computing for precision agriculture and water conservation
abstract: The modern global trend towards sustainable agricultures and efficient water resources management enforces smart irrigation systems. This study presents Soil Moisture-Based Intelligent Irrigation System based on loT sensors, cloud computing and AI based prediction model that is used to optimize the use of water in precision agriculture. Majority of which were calibrated volumetric water content (VWC) references to capacitive soil moisture probes that were introduced into agricultural zones and were monitored in real-time. The data provided by loT -enabled microcontrollers (Arduino with LoRa modules) was transmitted to an edge gateway where the signal was enhanced by noise removal and time-series smoothing prior to cloud upload. A Long ShortTerm Memory (LSTM) model was used to anticipate trends in soil moisture by using environmental data including rainfall, humidity, and temperature. Predictions were made and the system operated the solenoid valves in the areas where irrigation was necessary minimizing water wastage and increasing the efficiency. Findings have shown that the system kept the soil moisture level within a range of 2% of target desirable soil moisture levels with an average of 98.7% accuracy in all the irrigation. Water savings of 25-27% relative to manual techniques of irrigation were found using a comparative analysis, and node duty cycling brought in savings of the battery life of the devices of 65-70%. The dashboard on the cloud enabled farm owners to remotely supervise condition in the field, set alarms and operate irrigation. Generally, the idea to combine the incorporation of loT and AI produced significant efficiency gains in irrigation, water savings, and operational stability. This framework has the potential to be implemented across a very large scale in the agricultural sector particularly in water-stressed areas.

title: Deep Learning-Driven Soil Quality Analysis for Sustainable Crop Management
source_title: Proceedings 2025 2nd International Conference on Electronic Circuits and Signaling Technologies Icecst 2025
title_norm: deep learningdriven soil quality analysis for sustainable crop management
abstract: Evaluating soil quality is essential for sustainable agricultural practices, since it directly influences crop output and resource efficiency. Conventional soil analysis techniques are laborious, time-consuming, and sometimes insufficient for extensive applications, hence requiring automated and precise methodologies. This paper introduces a deep learning framework using a VGG16 Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for assessing soil quality via data obtained from IoTenabled sensors and remote sensing technologies. A dataset of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1 0, 0 0 0}$</tex> soil samples, classified by moisture content, nutrient composition, and texture, was used for model building. The model was trained on 80 % of the dataset, validated on 10 %, and tested on 10 %, with an accuracy of 99.71 %. The proposed method decreased soil categorization time by 40 % compared to traditional procedures, allowing quicker and more efficient studies across large agricultural regions. Real-time projections enabled enhanced irrigation and fertilisation methods, leading to a 22 % improvement in water efficiency and an 18 % decrease in fertilizer use. The findings illustrate the potential of deep learning to enhance precision agriculture via data-driven decision-making. Future efforts will focus on increasing the dataset and including multimodal sensor fusion to further improve model robustness and scalability.

title: Prototyping of Smart Irrigation System Using IoT Technology
source_title: 7th International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Information Engineering Technological Breakthrough for Greater New Life Iceeie 2021
title_norm: prototyping of smart irrigation system using iot technology
abstract: This research executes a development of prototype of smart irrigation system using IoT technology aiming to assist agriculture individual on reducing labor force and time to increase yield production as well as modernize traditional agriculture method. It is consisted of one controller and two sensor nodes communicate using star topology of Zigbee communication protocol. The system uses Xbee s2c module for data transferring from each sensor node to the controller. Each sensor node equips with sensors to collect significant parameters such as humidity, ambient temperature, soil moisture and solar radiation which influence crop’s production. All of the harvested data are presented on LCD display at the controller node for real-time monitoring and irrigation task based on soil moisture level. It also uploads data to cloud platform service (ThingSpeak) via internet enabled by Wi-Fi module (Node MCU) for further data analysis. The system has already been implemented in two greenhouses at Institute of Technology of Cambodia (ITC) and Royal University of Agriculture (RUA). As a consequence, the crops have been grown healthy with less effort and time requirement, thanks to the automatic irrigation system. In the future, data collection and control module will be improved using industrial-grade microcontroller on a solid surface mounted PCB module with Human Machine Interface (HMI) for the display to enhance user experience.

title: Intelligent Water Management System in Agricuture
source_title: 10th International Conference on Electrical Energy Systems Icees 2024
title_norm: intelligent water management system in agricuture
abstract: Agriculture holds a central role in India's food production and overall development. However, the reliance on monsoons for water can be unpredictable, necessitating the adoption of irrigation methods. The rise of Internet of Things (IoT) technology, significant strides have been made, especially in agriculture, offering promising solutions to sustainably feed a growing global population. This paper is dedicated to mitigating water scarcity in agriculture through the implementation of a microcontroller-based system. By eliminating the need for manual irrigation scheduling based on crop or soil conditions, this system streamlines the process. It incorporates various sensors to monitor essential elements like soil moisture, temperature, and air humidity. Automated irrigation is activated when soil moisture and temperature dip below pre-set thresholds, ensuring optimal water usage. This system proves particularly advantageous in regions with limited water resources, as it efficiently fulfils agricultural requirements while conserving water. In essence, the primary focus is on deploying smart irrigation techniques and automatic tank monitoring to enhance water usage efficiency. This approach promises to revolutionize agricultural practices, effectively addressing water crises and contributing to the advancement of the agricultural sector in the country.

title: Sensor based Automatic Irrigation System
source_title: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies Icefeet 2024
title_norm: sensor based automatic irrigation system
abstract: Due to scarcity of the water resource, the farmers expect a solution that changes the way to operate. Moreover, Intensive agricultural practices have adversely impacted soil quality, therefore it is necessary soil nutrient analysis for increasing farm productivity and environmental sustainability. Additionally, exponential population growth and enhancing demand, the farmers would require dedicated approach for irrigation to the land to achieve this demand. With advancement of latest technologies, there is scope to think about advancement in the irrigation system. Therefore, the paper presents sensor based automatic irrigation system. The condition of the soil is measured by soil moisture sensor which is already deployed in the field. Some threshold value is set, depending on the crop type. Based on the dry condition of soil, a notification is sent to the farmer’s mobile. Consequently, the pump would start to give water supply to the dry field. A prototype is developed to execute the proposed concept. The detailed methodology using flow chart is presented to give clear picture for researchers, academicians who are working in the agriculture field.
