title: Smart AgriTech with Machine Learning: Enhancing Crop Yield via Intelligent Recommendation and Irrigation System
source_title: International Conference on Emerging Trends and Innovations in ICT Icei 2026
title_norm: smart agritech with machine learning enhancing crop yield via intelligent recommendation and irrigation system
abstract: A fully intelligent agritech platform is developed using advanced machine learning techniques to improve the crop yield through smart irrigation and intelligent recommendations. An model for the recommendation of crops is incorporated where in the system indicates the best-fitting crops suited for a location depending on surroundings like soil condition, weather conditions, and the availability of water. It uses historical data sets to predict yield returns with high accuracy, facilitating optimized resource allocation, enhanced profitability, and environmentally friendly farming. The irrigation status system is driven by Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, which have a remarkable accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.96}$</tex>, facilitating accurate prediction and monitoring of irrigation needs. Particularly, the system forecasts whether irrigation is needed or not for the plant based on input features such as soil moisture, temperature, and weather conditions. For crop recommendation, Naive Bayes with 0.99 accuracy and Decision Tree with 0.97 accuracy are utilized to examine environmental conditions and recommend the most appropriate crops. Besides, XGBoost and Random Forest algorithms are utilized for highly accurate yield prediction and decision-making. These models process vast amounts of agricultural data at a large scale to reveal buried patterns and correlation that aid well-informed planning in agriculture. Model training and validation datasets utilized were accessed through Kaggle and contained detailed data about soil composition, weather conditions, types of crops, and irrigation levels to allow solid data-driven development. By incorporating a smart advisory mechanism, the system optimizes agronomic decision-making, facilitates precision agriculture, and ensures eco-efficient irrigation specific to crop requirements. This technology enables farmers to enhance productivity, safeguard food security, lower operational expenses, and preserve natural resources.

Water supplies became pollute and scarce. During the last years, the necessity to use water resources such as rivers, ground water and rain water efficiently has increased rapidly. Population growth, rapid urbanization and climate change have stressed water resources on the planet. The application of wireless soil-moisture sensor networks to detect water content in the soil can utilize water resources very efficiently. This will be more efficient in terms of the time in which the sensor will be excited and the quantity of water that will be used.

title: Remote Sensing-Based Model for Estimating Groundwater Pumping: Case Study of Irrigated Perimeter of the Medjerda Lower Valley, Tunisia
source_title: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo Spatial Information Iceogi 2023
title_norm: remote sensingbased model for estimating groundwater pumping case study of irrigated perimeter of the medjerda lower valley tunisia
abstract: The estimation of groundwater exploitation in arid and semi-arid countries such as Tunisia remains a challenging issue. In the Medjerda lower basin, water resources are overexploited due to Climate Change, anthropogenic pressures, and the intensification of irrigated areas. To address this, estimating spatially distributed crop water consumption is crucial for promoting efficient water management. This study aims to estimate volumes of groundwater pumping for irrigation in a citrus orchard area of the Medjerda Lower Valley basin using earth observation data as input of the SAtellite Monitoring of Irrigation (SAMIR) model based on the FAO-56 dual crop coefficient water balance model. The SAMIR model's simulated irrigation volumes were compared with the actual volumes of water that were supplied by farmers. The results showed significant difference between the simulated required volumes of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{1252074 \ \mathrm{m}^{3}}$</tex> and the declared amount of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$663 \ 882 \ \mathrm{m}^{3}$</tex>, indicating an estimated groundwater irrigation pumping of about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$239 \ 813 \ \mathrm{m}^{3}/\text{year}$</tex>. These findings confirm the feasibility of earth observation data for estimating irrigation groundwater pumping in water-scarce areas, and that they can be useful for decision-makers.

title: Machine Learning Approach in IoT-based Smart Irrigation: A Review for Sustainable Agriculture
source_title: Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Electronics and Sustainable Communication Systems Icesc 2025
title_norm: machine learning approach in iotbased smart irrigation a review for sustainable agriculture
abstract: With rising global food demand and increasing stress on freshwater resources, agriculture faces mounting pressure to optimize water use. Traditional irrigation methods are inefficient, often causing substantial water loss due to runoff, evaporation, and overwatering. This review highlights the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI), especially Machine Learning (ML), to revolutionize irrigation practices by enabling precision and water-efficient agriculture. Smart irrigation systems powered by ML leverage data from IoT sensors-monitoring soil moisture, humidity, temperature, and rainfall to automate water delivery based on real-time field conditions. Advanced models such as SVM, KNN, and CNNs help forecast water requirements, minimize wastage, and improve crop yield. It also addresses challenges like high system costs, inconsistent sensor data, and the need for farmer training. The study emphasizes the importance of integrating AI, affordable sensing technologies, and open data platforms to promote sustainable, climate-resilient agriculture and ensure optimal water usage in diverse agricultural environments.

title: Irrigation management systems of Dong Irrigation District based on GIS, MDS and AMS
source_title: 2011 International Conference on Electric Technology and Civil Engineering Icetce 2011 Proceedings
title_norm: irrigation management systems of dong irrigation district based on gis mds and ams
abstract: All of geographical information system (GIS), management decision-making system (MDS) and automatic monitoring system (AMS) are important signs of the modernization of irrigation management. Although these technologies have been applied in some irrigation districts, their functions have not been generally integrated systematically. The authors, taking Dong Irrigation District as an example, developed an integrated irrigation management system including GIS, MDS and AMS. This study focused on the integration of all functions of GIS, MDS and AMS, such as management of basic spatial datum, prediction of water requirement of crops, decision-making of water supply, monitoring of irrigation pump stations and canal system, evaluations of management system, etc. In particular, evaluations of management system can provide important feedback information for improving irrigation management decision-making.

title: Smart and Sustainable Irrigation Integrated with Threat Deterrence
source_title: International Conference on Emerging Technologies in Electronics and Green Energy Iceteg 2025
title_norm: smart and sustainable irrigation integrated with threat deterrence
abstract: This article presents the Smart and Sustainable Irrigation Integrated with Threat Deterrence (SSITD) system, an IoT-based agricultural solution that automates watering and preserves crops using intelligent methods. The primary objective is to optimize water usage while protecting crops from animals and birds through integrated sensor-based automation. Using real-time data from soil moisture sensors, the system initiates irrigation cycles only when necessary, particularly in areas with limited water supplies. Laser sensors detect animal infiltration in crop fields, while ultrasonic sensors are used to detect birds and safeguard crops from harm. The GSM module provides real-time alerts to farmers about irrigation status and security threats. An electric fence administers mild deterrence to prevent animal encroachment. Field validation demonstrates significant water consumption reduction, high accuracy in animal intrusion detection, and effective bird deterrence compared to conventional methods. This comprehensive approach increases crop productivity while conserving resources through sustainable precision agriculture.

title: Adaptive wireless sensor networks powered by hybrid energy harvesting for environmental monitoring
source_title: Iciafs 2012 Proceedings 2012 IEEE 6th International Conference on Information and Automation for Sustainability
title_norm: adaptive wireless sensor networks powered by hybrid energy harvesting for environmental monitoring
abstract: Due to the cost-effective nature and deployment flexibility of wireless sensor network (WSN), it has been extensively used in many real world applications. Sensor nodes are relatively inexpensive and capable of data processing and wireless communication with some level of intelligence, they play a key role in real world applications. Precision irrigation in agriculture is a key application of wireless sensor network. Typically, a sensor node is powered by its on-board battery source. This limitation fully or partially contributes to causing many problems in the network such as the loss of connectivity of a sensor node known as orphaned-node. Moreover, available number of sensor types in a sensor node is typically limited and it requires a significant modification in hardware and software interfaces to extend the number of sensor types. In this paper, we propose an adaptive sensor node system combining a flexible hardware prototype and innovative energy harvesting techniques to optimise the performance of the network operating in a large farming environment.

title: Arduino based soil moisture analyzer as an effective way for irrigation scheduling
source_title: 2018 IEEE 9th International Conference on Information and Automation for Sustainability Iciafs 2018
title_norm: arduino based soil moisture analyzer as an effective way for irrigation scheduling
abstract: Through the present study we vindicated the crop water requirement for eggplant by using Arduino based soil moisture investigator and compared the total water requirement with the quantity of water being applied by farmers to save such excess quantity of water being wasted by the farmers. Therefore a device was established in the Arduino platform in order to detect the soil moisture, as the moisture sensor shows only the resistance between the two probes. It was calibrated with direct moisture meter to obtain the moisture readings directly. Then selected egg plants were planted in two drip fixed fields in two different times. Such time variation in planting was maintained to facilitate the root study in one field before the irrigation of the test field. Hence, according to the measured root length the soil moisture sensors were inserted into the soil in the test field and plants were irrigated up to the field capacity by using the moisture detection. The measured quantity of water which is actually needed by an eggplant up to 108 days after planting was around 149.26 liter. Simultaneously an investigation was carried out to find the quantity of water being applied by farmers. Finally. The measured quantity of water being applied by the farmers was 604.8 liter and it is 4.05 times higher than actual water requirement. Therefore, by using this soil moisture sensing technique it is possible to save a huge amount of water.

source_title: Proceedings of the International Conference on Inventive Communication and Computational Technologies Icicct 2018
title_norm: iot based low cost smart irrigation system
abstract: One of the essential and basic services to survive on earth is Water. Recent time increasing the scarcity of water due to growing in population. So this is becoming as a universal obstacle. The old irrigation system which demands a lot of water, so it needs smart techniques for reducing the percentage of wasting available water for the irrigation. We have been seeing the increasing of huge demand for Internet of things in every domain from small and simple applications to large and complex applications. Practically implementation of a Smart Irrigation is very complex deal, but association with IoT using Smart wireless sensors it brings a great management system. The Humidity and Temperature Sensor sense the both water vapor content and temperature around the plant. The Soil Moisture Sensor sense the soil moisture of a plant, if water content is below minimum requirement then water will supply from water reservoir using relay and Ultrasonic sensor measures the water level of reservoir after that sends the data to ESP8266 NodeMCU. ESP8266 NodeMCU is a Microcontroller gets the data from smart wireless sensors, process the data and send to destination through A Message Queue Telemetry Transport (MQTT)protocol.

source_title: Proceedings of the International Conference on Inventive Computing and Informatics Icici 2017
title_norm: design and implementation of an automatic irrigation feedback control system based on monitoring of soil moisture
abstract: This paper deals with the development in agricultural activities like irrigation, soil temperature and moisture measurement using digital technologies and wireless sensors. Water is the heart of irrigation system and shortage of water is a growing issue for farmers. Water quantity needs to be checked for better productivity and sustainability of crops. Water regulation for different crops is different as insufficient or excessive water can be destructive for farming. An automatic wireless sensor based Irrigation Water Regulation support system is being developed. The proposed system estimates the water requirement for crops on the basis of soil moisture data gathered by several sensor nodes deployed in the field. Automation proved time and cost effective in a manner which is of great boon to the industry and as well as for entrepreneur in all the dimensions.

title: Sustainable Irrigation System Using Solar Panel Tracking and IoT Integration
source_title: Proceedings of the 2025 3rd International Conference on Inventive Computing and Informatics Icici 2025
title_norm: sustainable irrigation system using solar panel tracking and iot integration
abstract: Sustainable agriculture depends on effective water management, especially in areas with scarce energy and water resources. An IoT-based irrigation solar tracking system with a clever framing mechanism is presented in this paper. For automated water distribution, the system uses an ESP32 microcontroller to collect the real-time data from temperature and soil moisture sensors, and it turns on the irrigation pump when necessary. A timer-based solar panel is implemented to increase energy efficiency. Surplus energy is stored in the battery unit to ensure an uninterrupted system operation during nighttime or during the rainy season. The system is integrated with the Blynk IoT platform for remote monitoring and controlling, which enables farmers to receive live updates and also be able to adjust the operation of the system when needed from the mobile application. In addition to reducing water usage by up to 30%, the system's testing and simulation show that the solar panel's energy output is increased by 20-25% when compared to a static panel. These outcomes demonstrate how well the system supports intelligent farming methods in limited settings, thereby lowering energy and water waste.

title: Internet of things based smart irrigation using regression algorithm
source_title: 2017 International Conference on Intelligent Computing Instrumentation and Control Technologies Icicict 2017
title_norm: internet of things based smart irrigation using regression algorithm
abstract: The present scenario necessitates the utilization of water resources efficiently due to various reasons like population growth, rapid urbanization and climatic change. This has stressed for an effective management of water resources on our planet. The mismanagement of water used for irrigation not only results in shortage of water but also affects the agricultural production. Therefore it is necessary to optimize the water consumption by providing a monitor and control system for the irrigation process. The manual interpretation of soil water content shows inaccurate results. Also, the human interventions in monitoring the crops lead to wastage of time and energy. The proposed system aims to provide a sustainable solution by automatic monitor and control of irrigation process by using Internet of Things (IoT). In this paper, regression algorithm is used, which aids in the forecast of the amount of water required for the daily irrigation based on the data provided by various sensor devices. The forecasted information is made available on the mobile application (app), through which the current status of the agricultural field can be accessed. Henceforth this sensor network application will help to detect water content in the soil and aids in the smart utilization of water resources.

title: Implementing AI to Enhance Irrigation and Precision Application of Pesticides and Herbicides in Agriculture
source_title: Proceedings of 5th International Conference on Iot Based Control Networks and Intelligent Systems Icicnis 2024
title_norm: implementing ai to enhance irrigation and precision application of pesticides and herbicides in agriculture
abstract: The utilization of water, pesticides, and herbicides by producers is being transformed by AI. Precision cultivation enhances sustainability and efficiency. An AI-based irrigation and pesticide/herbicide targeting system is suggested in this paper. Machine learning, computer vision, and IoT sensors comprise the system. The system can distribute water and fertilizers in accordance with the requirements of the crop by monitoring real-time soil moisture, temperature, and insect activity. Machine learning algorithms can forecast optimal irrigation regimens and address insect infestations exclusively in drone-impacted areas, thereby reducing waste and environmental impact. Without affecting crop health or productivity, a pilot study decreased pesticide use by 25% and water usage by 30%. The AI-driven system enhances precision agriculture by promoting sustainable cultivation, reducing costs, and increasing efficiency.

title: Design and Implementation of Seasonal based Auto Irrigation System using Intelligent Controller
source_title: 7th International Conference on Inventive Computation Technologies Icict 2024
title_norm: design and implementation of seasonal based auto irrigation system using intelligent controller
abstract: To optimize the water usage in agriculture and improve the crop growth, FX5U intelligent based Seasonal Based Irrigation System (SBAIS) is introduced. Different sensors like moisture measurement sensors, Soil Moisture sensors, temperature sensors are used to collect information about the soil and environment to know the crop requirements. All the sensors are connected with the PLC input AI/DI ports with suitable signal conditioning hardware setup and the data are fed to the data memory of the intelligent controller. The AIML algorithm is used in the FX5U controller to analyze the sensors data and produces the optimal irrigation schedule and crop water needs. Python programming is used in FX5U controller to train the model with different seasonal inputs. The trained AIML model produces the desired and optimal output for drip irrigation system. This proposed system reduces the manual work involvement and improve the crop productivity and it mainly saves the water. Due to this invention, the water scarcity problems are reduced during the summer condition.

title: An IoT-based Water Management System for Precision Irrigation using AquaNet-S Model
source_title: Proceedings of 9th International Conference on Inventive Computation Technologies Icict 2026
title_norm: an iotbased water management system for precision irrigation using aquanets model
abstract: Effective water management has been a very important problem in the agricultural industry, especially in water-deficient areas. By combining both IoT-based and data-driven intelligent models (IMs) of irrigation optimization, this paper presents an intelligent model, which is called AquaNet-S, to optimize irrigation and crop productivity. In the system, the field-deployed IoT sensors such as temperature sensor, humidity sensor, soil moisture sensor, and water flow sensor are used in the system to gather real-time data of soil and the environment. The obtained data is sent through the wireless communication devices like Wi-Fi and LoRa to the central processing unit of the AquaNet-S model that processes the data to understand the content of the soil, weather conditions, and requirements of the crop to come up with the best irrigation times. The suggested system automatically manages autopilot irrigation pumps and solenoid valves to distribute the accurate amounts of water using the crop needs. Experimental findings show that there is a 30-40% decrease in the use of water as compared to the traditional irrigation techniques and the soil moisture is also maintained at optimal levels between 60-75% of major crops grown regions. The system was able to achieve an irrigation rate of about 92-96% and latency of real-time response of less than 2 seconds. Also, the field trials showed an increase in crop yield by 15- 20% owing to the fact that water was distributed in a timely manner and evenly. The web and mobile dashboard can also be integrated and farmers can follow irrigation and get alerts, thereby enabling them to make informed decisions. On the whole, the suggested model guarantees sustainable water resource management, reduces the level of water waste, and promotes precision agriculture based on the regional climatic conditions.

title: Design and Deployment Challenges of IoT-enabled Irrigation System for Sustainable Intercropping
source_title: Proceedings of 6th International Conference on Intelligent Communication Technologies and Virtual Mobile Networks Icicv 2025
title_norm: design and deployment challenges of iotenabled irrigation system for sustainable intercropping
abstract: Agriculture plays a vital role in global food security, economic stability, and sustainable development. Intercropping enhances productivity by optimizing resource use, promoting biodiversity, and reducing pest and disease risks. Efficient irrigation in intercropping systems remains a significant challenge due to the varying water requirements of different crops. title: Explainable AI for Smart Irrigation using Soil Moisture and Climate Data
source_title: Proceedings of 7th International Conference on Intelligent Communication Technologies and Virtual Mobile Networks Icicv 2026
title_norm: explainable ai for smart irrigation using soil moisture and climate data
abstract: Efficient planning of irrigation is very important for sustainable agriculture in Tamil Nadu as climate variability and growing water scarcity requires data-driven decision making. Conventional methods of scheduling irrigation are based on limited single station weather observations, does not consider spatial climate variability and even ignored soil heterogeneity often resulting in inaccurate estimates of water requirements, which are also not easily interpreted. This study focuses on proposing an explainable and spatially aware irrigation prediction system that incorporates multi-location satellite-derived climate data from the NASA POWER API) called POWER API, soil classification based on FAO framework of Food and Agriculture Organization International (FAO) and advanced machine learning regression models to predict irrigation requirements for a trajectory of days in litres per hectare. The area under study is Tamil Nadu, whole Each observation is collected at daily intervals establishing a complete data set of 54,810 observations over 30 spatial grid locations covering the period 2020-2024. Multiple regression models such as Linear Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest and XGBoost have been systematically analysed for ensuring robust model selection, to prevent bias induced by model dependence on a single method. Random Forest gave the highest overall performance with R2 value of 0.9999 with MAE of 279 L/ha and XGBoost performed best in terms of generalization with a cross validation R2 value of 0.9973. The reason for the high R2 values are explained to the structured nature of the data set, consistent environmental relationships, and feature engineering for the three spatial and temporal dimensions. Explainable Artificial Intelligence using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) that rainfall, longitude and temperature are the biggest predictors, but soil type has a significant moderating effect on water retention capacity. In addition, the system includes real-time simulation function to model dynamic irrigation demand, which can improve the practicality of the use. The framework proposed is to support precision irrigation, promote transparency and trust in the AI-driven recommendations, and contribute to sustainable water resource management in the smart agriculture systems.

title: IoT-Driven Soil Moisture Monitoring for Optimizing Irrigation
source_title: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Cybernetics Technology and Applications Icicyta 2024
title_norm: iotdriven soil moisture monitoring for optimizing irrigation
abstract: As the global population continues to rise, the demand for higher food production exerts increasing pressure on traditional irrigation systems, which often lack the precision and efficiency required to meet modern agricultural demands. This growing challenge imposes innovative solutions, such as the integration of Internet of Things (IoT) technology into agriculture, which has led to the creation of smart irrigation systems. These advanced systems utilize IoT-enabled soil moisture monitoring sensors to collect real-time data on key environmental variables such as soil moisture, temperature, humidity, and other atmospheric conditions. Through this data, farmers gain actionable insights that allow them to automate and optimize irrigation, eliminating the need for manual intervention. This study explores into the benefits of IoT-based soil moisture monitoring systems, focusing on the capabilities for remote management, automation, and adaptability to climatic conditions. Key features include real-time data for on-demand and timed watering, as well as the simulation of rainfall patterns, which ensure optimal soil moisture levels. These technologies do not only help conserve water resources and reduce labor requirements but also promote sustainable farming practices by minimizing resource wastage. By improving irrigation efficiency and enhancing crop growth reliability, IoT-driven systems contribute to addressing global food security challenges, ensuring the sustainability of agricultural practices in the face of population growth.

title: IoT-Enabled Optimized Irrigation System using Soil Moisture
source_title: International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems Iciics 2023
title_norm: iotenabled optimized irrigation system using soil moisture
abstract: Agriculture serves as a crucial foundation for developing any growing nation, being the primary source of sustenance and employment. However, in the face of a rapidly changing world, the agricultural sector must adapt to continue fulfilling its role in supporting the country. With climate change altering rainfall patterns, the traditional knowledge that has been passed down through generations for predicting rainfall is no longer adequate for ensuring efficient farming practices. This can result in situations where crops experience either inadequate hydration or excessive irrigation. Under-hydration can be detrimental to crop survival, while over-irrigation poses issues with soil aeration and salinity. The consequences of over-irrigation include increased weed growth and the development of diseases that may shorten plants’ lifespans and diminish overall tree health and vitality. To address these challenges, it becomes essential to adopt innovative techniques that conserve water during the irrigation process. In the proposed system, both soil moisture levels using a soil moisture sensor and the probability of precipitation over the field - fetched from the weather API - are continuously monitored. By combining data from these factors, an optimized decision is made to ensure the plants receive water only when necessary. This approach aims to enhance watering efficiency while promoting optimal plant growth and sustainability.

title: Automation in drip irrigation using IOT devices
source_title: 2017 4th International Conference on Image Information Processing Iciip 2017
title_norm: automation in drip irrigation using iot devices
abstract: Internet of things (IOT) has become very popular and it is growing rapidly in the field of communication. This paper describes the control and monitor of drip irrigation process using IOT and Image processing techniques. The automated system includes a database to analyze the water requirement of plant. The database contains a predefined soil moisture values and it is editable according to the soil type of the place where we implement this system. Different types of soils will have different moisture values and moisture values will also change in accordance with the climate. Our proposed system uses a soil moisture sensor to take the soil moisture reading from the field in real time to water them in an automated way by switching the drip service ON/OFF using an android App. Most of the times infected plants are identified by the change in color of the leaves. A camera is used to take pictures of the plants leaves and image processing algorithms are implemented on those captured image for further steps. A database is used for comparison between the original and real time image, which results in identifying the diseased plant or part of plant. Thus, our proposed system is made effective and cost efficient.

title: IoT-Driven Smart Irrigation System for Optimizing Water Use in Agriculture
source_title: Proceedings of 7th International Conference on Inventive Material Science and Applications Icima 2025
title_norm: iotdriven smart irrigation system for optimizing water use in agriculture
abstract: Water shortages and the deactivation of irrigation practices are still significant challenges in modern agriculture, especially in dry and semi-dry areas. To address these problems, this article presents the design and implementation of an IoT-operated smart irrigation system aimed at optimizing water use through real-time soil moisture monitoring and automatic control. The proposed system integrates a cloud-based data platform to monitor the soil condition using a reliable soil moisture sensor, a micro-controller, and cloud-based data platforms to automate water distribution accordingly. By using a threshold-based algorithm, the system ensures that water is supplied only when the soil moisture level drops below a predetermined threshold, which reduces water waste. The architecture allows for real-time data collection and remote monitoring through an IoT dashboard, simplifying management for farmers and reducing labor requirements. A prototype was developed and tested in a controlled environment to validate system functionality. The results indicate that the system effectively maintains soil moisture at optimal levels, promoting plant health and achieving a 30% water savings compared to traditional manual irrigation methods. The system is suitable for scalability, is cost-effective, and works well for small- to medium-sized farms, especially in areas with limited water access. In addition, its modular design allows for future improvements, such as integration with weather forecasts and machine learning algorithms for future irrigation planning. This work contributes to sustainable agriculture by promoting smart agricultural techniques that improve water conservation and resource efficiency, supporting farmers in adapting to changing climates and ensuring a stable food supply.

abstract: Modern agriculture must use modern approaches to address issues like market volatility, water scarcity, and climate unpredictability because of the sector's crucial position in economies worldwide, particularly the Indian subcontinent. Purpose of this research is to close gap by using machine learning (ML) algorithms for predicting soil types and suggest appropriate crops, fertilizers, and irrigation techniques to increase agricultural output. The proposed methodology involves utilizing key input parameters, including pH value, organic matter content, NPK values, and district-level data, to predict soil types. Subsequently, the identified soil type, along with additional parameters such as NPK values, organic matter, and water availability, will inform the crop recommendation model. Further, the selected crop, in conjunction with data on water availability, soil type, and water requirements, will guide the irrigation recommendation system. Moreover, the paper extends its scope to fertilizer recommendation, utilizing input variables such as NPK values, pH level, soil type, and specific crop information. This comprehensive approach aims to empower farmers with precise and tailored guidance, optimizing agricultural practices and mitigating challenges arising from unpredictable weather conditions and resource limitations. The project aims to achieve a comprehensive framework using ML techniques for categorization and prediction algorithms. The research aims to support sustainable and effective agricultural practices by advancing crop prediction and fertilizer recommendation through the exploration of several algorithms, including Decision trees, SVM, Random-forest (RF), and k-NN.

title: A Novel Federated Learning using Deformable Convolutional GRU Framework for Smart Irrigation in Next-Gen Agriculture with Encryption
source_title: Proceedings of 8th International Conference on Intelligent Sustainable Systems Iciss 2026
title_norm: a novel federated learning using deformable convolutional gru framework for smart irrigation in nextgen agriculture with encryption
abstract: Smart irrigation plays a crucial role in farming, where real-time sensor information and smart decision-making technology improve the sustainability and accuracy. Within this framework, Federated Learning (FL) provides a robust solution to enhance irrigation strategies collaboratively without revealing their confidential data. This strategy guarantees that the agricultural information stays secure, both during processing and transmission, when paired with secure encryption methods, which promote the ethical and safe digital advancement in the agricultural sector. However, the intelligent irrigation is hindered by various drawbacks associated with current centralized methods. These systems analyze large volumes of raw data in a central location, which heightens the chances of unauthorized access and breaches of farmers' trust. Hence, in this work, a novel FL-based network is introduced for smart irrigation in next-gen agriculture. In the beginning, the required data from the Internet of Things (IoT) sensors is collected and then subjected to Fully Homomorphic Encryption with Polynomial Arithmetic (FHE-PA) for encrypting and preserving the privacy of the data. Further, the encrypted data are subjected to Federated Learning using Deformable Convolutional Gated Recurrent Unit (FL-DCGRU) for decision making in the irrigation process. In the end, the developed framework is compared with the conventional models to ensure its effectiveness.

title: A Machine Learning-Driven IoT Architecture for Intelligent Irrigation and Fertigation in Horticultural Crops
source_title: 7th International Conference on Mobile Computing and Sustainable Informatics Icmcsi 2026
title_norm: a machine learningdriven iot architecture for intelligent irrigation and fertigation in horticultural crops
abstract: Effective management of water and nutrients is critical to improving productivity and sustainability in horticultural crop production systems that are experiencing increased climate variability, and limitations in water and nutrient resources. This paper presents an Internet of Things (IoT) architecture driven by Machine Learning (ML) for intelligent irrigation and fertigation management that is specific to horticultural systems. The proposed framework integrates a real-time multi-sensor network of soil moisture, soil temperature, soil electrical conductivity (EC), soil pH, ambient humidity, and vapor-pressure deficit (VPD) sensors with a NodeMCU microcontroller cloud data infrastructure. A supervised learning model based on the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm performs multi-class irrigation decision-making, placing water requirements in three categories: no irrigation, light irrigation, and heavy irrigation. The developed model achieved a testing accuracy of 95.0%, along with additional metrics that provided strong performance benchmarks including a macro-average F1-score of 0.94, and a ROC-AUC score of 0.97, showing high reliability for prediction at the field level. An anomaly detection module provides operational safety by identifying sensor drift, pipeline leakage, and actuator failure to entrain an automated fail-safe mode. The irrigation management system accommodates dynamically changing environmental dynamics by extending the data acquisition period and periodically retraining the model. The experimental research undertaken in agricultural fields of horticulture indicates increased water-use efficiency, decreased fertilizer consumption, and improved nutrient uniformity as opposed to standard irrigation based on rules. Thus, this study illustrates that the coupling of IoT sensing technology with intelligent machine-learning control is possibly disruptive for the future of precision sustainable horticulture.

title: Cloud-Based Precision Irrigation System: Optimizing Water Usage With Real-Time Environmental And Crop Factor Data
source_title: 2025 International Conference on Next Generation Computing Systems Intelligent System for Sustainable Development Icngcs 2025 Conference Proceedings
title_norm: cloudbased precision irrigation system optimizing water usage with realtime environmental and crop factor data
abstract: Global freshwater resources are diminishing, and water scarcity is becoming a critical issue; there is a pressing need for efficient irrigation in agriculture. In India, nearly 40-50% of water is lost due to inefficient irrigation practices. Over or underwatering can hinder plant growth and reduce crop yield. The current research employs IoT to enable precision irrigation by utilizing meteorological data obtained in real-time, in addition to cloud analytics to regulate water utilization. Water requirement calculation of the considered plant crop (potato) is done by regularly monitoring soil moisture data and evapotranspiration rates. The sensor data are pushed into the digital ocean cloud platform, where various parameters like moisture level thresholds, humidity levels, temperature, Evapotranspiration rate, and precipitation levels obtained from the OpenMeteo API are used to make watering decisions. The system utilizes the predefined crop factor data and the seed sown date to calculate the water in liters for the given area dynamically. The water quantity in litres is then communicated to the main controller. The main controller actuates the motor for watering purposes based on pipe parameters. Calculated watering enhances future water resource scheduling and helps the users analyze water trend requirements for a given plant type, leading to sustainable agricultural practices.

source_title: 5th Biennial International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering Icnte 2023
title_norm: design and fabrication of iot based agricultural automation system
abstract: The paper illustrates the use of smart devices and digitization to achieve agricultural process automation and increased yield of crops. Crops need fertilizers in the form of NP-K and water in a specific quantity and time. Current process of watering and adding fertilizers to specific plants is closely studied and correlated data on growth rates and fertilizer requirement is collected. This data is integrated into the smart Fertigation system which uses multiple sensors and smart devices. This system is then used to carry out controlled drip irrigation-based fertilization and irrigation of crops. An experimental setup for the same is deployed in a lab like environment using sensors to monitor parameters such as pH level of the soil, TDS values, temperature, humidity at a given time of the day, Arduino based actuator circuit is deployed for remote operations and control systems and additionally the remote data collection/control is enabled using Python and Google APIs. This fully functional IoT fertigation system collected data as illustrated in the paper. A correlation is drawn between the sensor actual data and control parameters of fertilizer and water supplied to the soil. This paper evaluates the viability of such a system in a controlled environment and further scaling of this system for farmers benefit to autonomously manage large land parcels based on weather data and soil characteristics.

abstract: The project involves the design and development of an autonomous irrigation sprinkler robot to optimize water usage in agriculture. This robot employs advanced sensors to continuously monitor soil moisture and environmental conditions, ensuring plants receive water only when necessary. Mounted on a mobile platform and equipped with a precision sprinkler system, it can traverse different terrains while distributing water efficiently based on real-time sensor data. A built-in control system analyzes this data to determine the optimal timing and duration of irrigation, significantly reducing water wastage and promoting healthier plant growth. title: A systematic review of GIS-based landslide Hazard Mapping on Determinant Factors from International Databases
source_title: 3rd International Conference on Advanced Science and Engineering Icoase 2020
title_norm: a systematic review of gisbased landslide hazard mapping on determinant factors from international databases
abstract: The landslide could severely affect infrastructure, irrigation systems, soil fertility, river and streams, and settlements. Both human-made and natural phenomena contribute to landslide hazards, and therefore a comprehensive assessment of landslide susceptibility is essential to its mitigation actions. Nowadays, geographical information systems and remote sensing in combination with modeling techniques have widely been used for assessment and mapping the susceptibility of the landslide. This study contains a review of 20 scientific articles on the spatial-statistical analysis of landslide susceptibility in the last ten years. The papers were reviewed for the locations of the case study, effective parameters used, and the results' validation. The review indicates the case studies were mostly for Asian countries, and this point was obtained that some vulnerable regions had sufficiently been studied. Various causative factors were used for spatial analysis and modeling of landslide susceptibility assessment where slope, lithology, curvature, and distance to rivers were used in most studies. This review concludes that for spatial dimension evaluation of the landslide, it is important to study a comprehensive set of both natural and anthropogenic factors. This review also provides useful information that can help future studies and serve as a resource for understanding the techniques used to manage this important natural hazard.

title: Predictive Water Supply Optimization Using Sensor Data, Machine Learning, and Weather Forecasts
source_title: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Emerging Computing and Intelligent Technologies Icoecit 2026
title_norm: predictive water supply optimization using sensor data machine learning and weather forecasts
abstract: Global warming and climate change are key contributors to water scarcity. Consequently, judicious management of water resources is essential for enduring sustainability. Agriculture is a significant consumer of water among several large-scale industries. The water utilised in agriculture has become polluted and is unfit for usage. Therefore, enhancing water management techniques for agricultural irrigation is imperative. This work introduces an automated irrigation system that employs real-time soil sensor data to predict the water management approach. Conversely, the decision-making function has been refined, and the weather conditions have been evaluated prior to initiating the water supply. The decision-making function requires anticipating the water treatment strategy and forthcoming weather conditions, and the Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) system has been trained to effectively predict both variables. A pre-processing strategy for the soil moisture sensor dataset has been proposed to improve its efficacy for training with machine learning algorithms. The assessments have been executed and a simulation has been carried out. The performance results demonstrate that the proposed weather prediction method employing ANN attains more accuracy compared to Support Vector Machines (SVM). Additionally, the period for training and decision-making of the system has been evaluated, indicating that choices may be made in a fraction of a second. The training period is considered sufficient, necessitating only one session of training on location-specific data.

title: An Intelligent Autonomous Robot for Precision Irrigation based on Soil Condition Monitoring
source_title: Proceedings of 9th International Conference on Trends in Electronics and Informatics Icoei 2026
title_norm: an intelligent autonomous robot for precision irrigation based on soil condition monitoring
abstract: An automated smart irrigation and monitoring system was developed to support sustainable agriculture through real-time sensing, wireless communication, and controlled water delivery. Environmental and soil parameters were continuously acquired using a soil moisture sensor, humidity and temperature sensor, and an ultrasonic sensor for distance-based monitoring. The collected data were processed through an Arduino-based control unit, and irrigation decisions were generated using threshold-driven logic to ensure that watering was performed only when required. A motor driver interface was employed to activate the DC water pump safely and efficiently, while a battery-powered supply was utilized to enable portable field operation. System status and sensor readings were transmitted through Bluetooth communication and were displayed on a smartphone terminal to support remote supervision and timely user awareness. Experimental validation was carried out using a functional prototype, and stable real-time monitoring was achieved with consistent sensor updates. Performance evaluation indicated satisfactory accuracy, rapid response time, acceptable battery utilization, moderate speed, and high stability during repeated operational cycles. Water wastage was reduced by ensuring irrigation activation based on actual soil condition rather than fixed schedules. The reliable integration of sensing, decision-making, communication, and actuation was demonstrated, and the developed system was found suitable for precision irrigation applications in smart farming environments.

title: IoT-based Smart Irrigation Model for Precision Agriculture using ESP8266 and Soil Moisture Analysis
source_title: Proceedings of the 4th International Conference on Intelligent Computing Information and Control Systems Icoiics 2025
title_norm: iotbased smart irrigation model for precision agriculture using esp8266 and soil moisture analysis
abstract: Water management is one of the biggest challenges in agriculture today. Many farmers still follow fixed irrigation schedules without checking the actual needs of the soil or the weather. This often causes water wastage or overwatering, which can harm both crops and the environment. To tackle this problem, we introduce a smart irrigation system that makes watering crops easier and more efficient. The system uses affordable microcontrollers like ESP32/ESP8266 along with sensors that measure soil moisture, temperature, humidity, rainfall, and soil pH. It can work automatically or be controlled by farmers through a mobile app or a web platform. With the help of machine learning, the system studies past data and current field conditions to decide the right amount of water required. Farmers also receive regular soil health updates and instant alerts whenever something unusual happens. In addition, the system keeps track of water flow, prevents overirrigation, and detects pump failures. It is compatible with both drip and sprinkler methods, making it useful for different types and sizes of farms. Overall, this smart irrigation system is affordable, easy to use, and scalable. It helps farmers save water, reduce labor, improve crop yield, and move towards more sustainable farming practices.

ABSTRACT: Water management is one of the biggest challenges in agriculture today. Many farmers still follow fixed irrigation schedules without checking the actual needs of the soil or the weather. This often causes water wastage or overwatering, which can harm both crops and the environment. To tackle this problem, we introduce a smart irrigation system that makes watering crops easier and more efficient. The system uses affordable microcontrollers like ESP32/ESP8266 along with sensors that measure soil moisture, temperature, humidity, rainfall, and soil pH. It can work automatically or be controlled by farmers through a mobile app or a web platform. With the help of machine learning, the system studies past data and current field conditions to decide the right amount of water required. Farmers also receive regular soil health updates and instant alerts whenever something unusual happens. In addition, the system keeps track of water flow, prevents overirrigation, and detects pump failures. It is compatible with both drip and sprinkler methods, making it useful for different types and sizes of farms. Overall, this smart irrigation system is affordable, easy to use, and scalable. It helps farmers save water, reduce labor, improve crop yield, and move towards more sustainable farming practices.

title: Low-Cost Fog Computing Platform for Soil Moisture Management
title_norm: lowcost fog computing platform for soil moisture management
abstract: Agriculture is experiencing a process of modernization enabled by Information and Communications Technology. This process enables improvement in decision-making processes on activities such as planting spacing, fertilization, and irrigation. The amount of water in the soil is an essential factor for the development of any crop, and it affects productivity, cost, and sustainability. Enhanced monitoring of soil moisture enables the timely reaction to undesirable moisture states and thus avoids negative effects on crops. In this direction, this paper presents a platform that leverages Internet of Things and Edge Computing to monitor soil moisture through sensors, data communication between sensors and edge devices, and an Analytics-as-a-Service cloud that provides analysis of the collected data in the form of a density map of soil moisture, indicating which areas should be irrigated with greater or lesser frequency. A small-scale evaluation of the platform deployed in a rural area shows that the proposed platform achieves similar levels of accuracy than conventional measurement methods without requiring the presence of humans on the field.

title: Cloud-Based IoT and Machine Learning System for Real-Time Monitoring and Forecasting of Crop Water Demand Under Climate Change Conditions
source_title: 2025 IEEE 4th International Conference for Advancement in Technology Iconat 2025
title_norm: cloudbased iot and machine learning system for realtime monitoring and forecasting of crop water demand under climate change conditions
abstract: Climate change is worsening changes in precipitation and temperature, affecting precise predictions of agricultural water requirements a vital element for sustainable farming. Conventional systems frequently struggle to adjust to changing environmental circumstances, resulting in ineffective watering methods and loss of resources. This proposed study presents a cloud-based Internet of Things and machine learning architecture that combines real-time sensor data, cloud computing, and a hybrid LSTM-XGBoost model to improve the precision of water demand forecasting. The system identifies temporal and non-linear correlations in environmental factors, higher than traditional approaches. The experimental evaluation indicates that the proposed system attains a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.14, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.09, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{2}}$</tex> value of 0.97, outperforming the performance of baseline models such as multiple linear regression (MLR) and support vector regression (SVR). The architecture guarantees scalability, minimal latency, and strong performance across various climate conditions. This approach provides enhanced accuracy, real-time processing, and practical applicability for precision irrigation compared to current studies. The results facilitate data-informed decision-making in climate-resilient agriculture.

title: IoT-Based Agriculture Farm Monitoring System and Development of Plant Leaf Disease Detection Using Deep Neural Network
source_title: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing Computation Electronics Power and Telecommunication Iconscept 2024 Proceedings
title_norm: iotbased agriculture farm monitoring system and development of plant leaf disease detection using deep neural network
abstract: Throughout history, agriculture or farming has played a vital role in human civilization by providing people's fundamental necessities and significant contributions to a country's economy. Although small-scale smart farming has started in a few nations, it has yet to be adopted scientifically globally. The rapid growth of the world population along with urbanization has rendered modern agriculture increasingly essential day by day. Towards multi-domain modernization, the Internet of Things (IoT) technology is a developing paradigm that aims to link many smart physical parameters in smart agriculture. In this paper, an IoT-based smart agricultural farm monitoring system prototype has been proposed which has been designed considering different environmental parameters. Additionally, image processing-based plant disease detection model has been developed in two different methods. The system incorporates various sensors, actuators, and a microcontroller to monitor and control temperature, humidity, soil moisture, and rainfall. It also includes a water pump motor for automated irrigation where a Wi-Fi module allows remote monitoring and controlled by a developed smartphone app. To validate, the proposed hardware model was simulated using Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools. There have been notable outcomes observed on temperature, humidity, soil moisture, and other monitoring parameters data reading from LCD. Also, deep learning-based image processing algorithm has been proposed using Feature extraction and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) methods and achieved a high accuracy of about 96%-98% in plant disease detection. The overall proposed system offers improved resource utilization and smart agricultural practices for expanded functionalities and long-term sustainability to ensure food security for the growing population.

title: Agro-tech: A digital model for monitoring soil and crops using internet of things (IOT)
source_title: Iconstem 2017 Proceedings 3rd IEEE International Conference on Science Technology Engineering and Management
title_norm: agrotech a digital model for monitoring soil and crops using internet of things iot
abstract: The various advancements made in numerous domains using new technologies are seen in many real time applications. Yet, the application of these technologies involved in the field of agriculture still remains a challenging task. The main aim of this paper is to propose a wireless sensor network technology in agronomy, which can show the path to the rural farming community to enhance some of the traditional techniques. This paper proposes an IOT application named `AGRO-TECH' that will be used to record, store and update the activities of various sensors which is accessible by farmers to keep track of his field details in terms of soil and crop monitoring. The activities such as soil moisture, level of ph., temperature, humidity, light dependent resistance, water level are monitored and observed by different types of sensors that are included in the proposed system. These sensors collectively combine the information that analyses to increase the yield of crop production. Based on the threshold value of soil moisture sensor the sensor relay triggers either the motor or the irrigation sprinkler to mitigate the impact of water scarcity by the monitoring of water level sensor in the tank and also the temperature sensor. Thus essential information about soil, crop and other environmental factors will be sent and updated to farmers through our proposed system methodology.

title: Integrating Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) into Modern Agrometerologica Approach for Precise, Real-Time Prediction in Crop Water
source_title: Proceedings of the 4th International Conference on Smart Electronics and Communication Icosec 2023
title_norm: integrating unmanned aerial vehicles uavs into modern agrometerologica approach for precise realtime prediction in crop water
abstract: A novel method for enhancing agrometeorological forecasts by incorporating Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) into the existing framework for accurate, real-time assessment of agricultural water requirements is proposed in this research work. When combined with agrometeorological modeling techniques, UAV-collected high-resolution, multispectral data has the potential to provide precise, timely information on agricultural water needs. This link may assist farmers and others with an interest in agriculture make more informed decisions about where and how to use irrigation water. Researchers propose using UAV-based remote sensing, weather station integration, and agrometeorological modeling to estimate the amount of water crops require. Early findings indicate that the integrated method has the potential to provide accurate forecasts promptly. The implications of this study's findings for precision agriculture are significant, especially in terms of fostering water-efficient management techniques. In the future, the prediction system will be refined and utilized in a wider range of agricultural contexts.

title: IoT based Automated Irrigation System for Aquaponics and Land Farming
source_title: Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Smart Electronics and Communication Icosec 2025
title_norm: iot based automated irrigation system for aquaponics and land farming
abstract: To monitor essential environmental parameters in real time, an IoT based smart irrigation system is proposed. pH and TDS sensors in aquaponics systems ensure that the water quality maintains itself at ideal levels for fish and plants, encouraging effective nutrient absorption and water recirculation. In land farming, soil moisture and NPK sensors provide precise data to enable precision irrigation and fertilization. Based on threshold-based decision-making and predictive analytics, the system dynamically triggers water pumps and actuators to regulate irrigation cycles. Cloud integration stores and analyzes historical data, enhancing system reliability and optimizing performance through data-driven insights. Real-time remote monitoring enables farmers to control and manage the system from anywhere, ensuring timely intervention and improved operational efficiency. The system’s performance is enhanced by predictive analytics models that forecast soil moisture and plant growth, enabling adaptive irrigation schedules. Fault detection mechanisms ensure system reliability by preventing sensor drift, communication failures, and power disruptions. By addressing challenges such as sensor calibration, power consumption, and system redundancy, this IOT-based irrigation system ensures consistent and accurate operation. It promotes sustainable agriculture by reducing water waste, lowering energy consumption, and improving overall crop health. The integration of IOT technologies in Aquaponics and land farming offers a scalable, efficient, and environmentally friendly solution for modern agricultural practices.

title: Fuzzy-based Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory (f-BiLSTM) based Interpretable Framework for Soil Nutrient Analysis in Precision Agriculture
source_title: Proceedings of 5th International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking Icpcsn 2025
title_norm: fuzzybased bidirectional long short term memory fbilstm based interpretable framework for soil nutrient analysis in precision agriculture
abstract: The escalating global demand for food and water, driven by a rapidly growing population, has intensified interest in precision agriculture. To meet this rising demand, farmers require reliable access to both water resources and arable land. However, the scarcity of these critical resources necessitates a fundamental shift in agricultural practices to enable more efficient utilization. Precision irrigation has emerged as a vital approach to achieving sustainable agriculture, empowering farmers to maximize crop yields while minimizing the use of essential resources. The integration of computer vision algorithms has led to the development of advanced irrigation models that emphasize water conservation. Nevertheless, the limited adaptability of these models hampers their effectiveness in regions with highly variable and unpredictable climatic conditions. In response to this challenge, this study presents a novel intelligent irrigation framework—Fuzzy-based Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (f-BiLSTM). This system harnesses the power of deep learning and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies to enable intelligent and efficient water management tailored for modern agricultural applications. A robust feedback mechanism is incorporated to maintain consistent performance across diverse weather conditions and geographical regions, at any given time. Experimental results clearly demonstrate that the f-BiLSTM model significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art irrigation systems in terms of water-use efficiency, establishing it as a highly effective solution for next-generation sustainable farming.

title: A MQTT-based Soil Moisture Level Notification System for a Smart Farm
source_title: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications Icpea 2021
title_norm: a mqttbased soil moisture level notification system for a smart farm
abstract: Smart irrigation is among the IoT smart farming practices deemed important in optimizing the ever-growing need for farm produce given the climate change and other farm produce affecting events e.g., COVID-19. In this paper we aim at enhancing the existing technology in smart farming by proposing some insight towards developing an easy-to-use tool. The tool helps irrigation farmers in making informed decisions on their water sprinkler placement for maintaining the recommended soil water moisture contents for their farm. Our framework notifies the farmer when the sprinklers rearrangement is due based on the farm’s soil moisture level readings. Our work defines the optimal computational parameter values for the strategic sprinkler deployment and introduces the required instruments and set up procedure. We demonstrate the implementation and user-friendly output of the apparatus with a display showing the actionable soil moisture information. Such results will provide the very critical information needed by a smart irrigation farmer to make informed decisions about their farm based on its soil water moisture contents.

title: Cloud-based internet of things approach for smart irrigation system: Design and implementation
source_title: Proceedings 2020 International Conference on Promising Electronic Technologies Icpet 2020
title_norm: cloudbased internet of things approach for smart irrigation system design and implementation
abstract: Water plays a significant role in the economic development of countries. The agriculture sector is the most water-consuming; this sector consumes 69% of the freshwater. However, farmers often use traditional irrigation systems to water their crops. These systems are ineffective and consume a IoT of time and effort, mainly when several fields are distributed in different geographical regions. Therefore, employing smart irrigation techniques will significantly overcome these problems. This paper proposes an intelligent irrigation framework based on Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) and Internet of Things (IoT) cloud services. The proposed system consists of three main components; the WSN, the control unit, and cloud services. Arduino Uno and XBee ZigBee modules are combined to gather sensors data and send them wirelessly to the control unit. YL-69 sensor is used to monitor the soil moisture. Raspberry Pi is utilized to gather data, process them, provide the proper decision, and transfer them to ThingSpeak IoT cloud. In the cloud, the data collected from the system is stored to create instance visualization of live data and send alerts. This allows farmers to monitor the status of crops and make the required decisions. After inspecting the prototype, many challenges are posed for future work.

title: Machine Learning-Based Weekly Evapotranspiration Prediction and Monitoring in Rice Fields Using MODIS in Thailand
source_title: 2025 8th International Conference on Robotic Systems and Applications Icrsa 2025
title_norm: machine learningbased weekly evapotranspiration prediction and monitoring in rice fields using modis in thailand
abstract: Accurate estimation of evapotranspiration (ET) is essential for optimizing irrigation in rice fields, particularly under increasing climate variability. This study presents a machine learning-based approach for predicting weekly ET using MODIS satellite data and ground-truth eddy covariance (EC) measurements collected from a rice field in Roi Et province, Thailand. MODIS vegetation and surface indices were used as inputs to six machine learning models, including Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Linear Regression. The EC system, which captures ET every second, was aggregated to match the 8-day MODIS ET product for validation. Results show that the Random Forest model achieved the highest accuracy during the 2020 rice-growing season <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}^{2}=0.915$</tex>, RMSE = 2.98 mm/week), while performance dropped in 2021 and in the combined dataset due to the absence of data between cropping periods. Feature importance analysis revealed that NDVI was most influential in 2020, LST in 2021, and EVI in the combined model-indicating seasonal variability in key predictors. The findings demonstrate the robustness of ensemble models for capturing ET dynamics and emphasize the need for seasonal-aware modeling approaches. This study highlights the potential of MODIS-based machine learning models as cost-effective, scalable tools for improving water resource management and supporting sustainable rice production in Thailand.

title: Smart Irrigation: Revolutionizing Water Management in Agriculture for Sustainable Practices and Improved Crop Yield
source_title: Proceedings of the 2023 6th International Conference on Recent Trends in Advance Computing Icrtac 2023
title_norm: smart irrigation revolutionizing water management in agriculture for sustainable practices and improved crop yield
abstract: An inventive method of managing water in agriculture, smart irrigation makes use of automation, sensors, and technology to maximize water utilization and minimize waste. As water scarcity becomes a greater worry and agricultural practices need to be sustainable, smart irrigation is becoming a vital tool for farmers all over the world. Farmers would be able to better manage water resources with the help of the proposed smart irrigation systems, which would provide them real-time data on soil moisture, weather, and crop water needs. By using that data, farmers may optimize water usage and minimize water loss by making well-informed decisions regarding watering schedules and amounts. Increased crop yield, reduced water consumption, and cost savings are just a few of the many benefits that farmers may reap from smart irrigation systems. Smart irrigation systems are able to automatically modify watering schedules and amounts to suit the unique requirements of individual crops by employing sensors that track the weather and the amount of moisture in the soil. This leads to less energy and fertilizer use and increased crop quality and yield. Smart irrigation systems can lower labor costs and boost farm profitability in addition to increasing crop yield and using less water. Farmers may save time and energy by automating their irrigation systems, which allows them to irrigate crops more precisely and at the proper times. This may result in lower expenses, higher output, and better environmental effects. Another sustainable technique that encourages water resource saving is smart irrigation. It is transforming the way that water is managed in agriculture. Smart irrigation systems will continue to advance through further research and development, becoming more widely available, affordable, and conducive to sustainable farming practices that will increase crop output.

title: Precision Agriculture using Internet of Things and Machine Learning
source_title: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication ICSC 2023
title_norm: precision agriculture using internet of things and machine learning
abstract: The agriculture industry is facing a significant challenge due to poor water management, resulting in a considerable decline in crop production. A lot of water used in irrigation is wasted due to inadequate management practices. The inefficient irrigation systems often have poor water flow control, leading to over-extraction of groundwater, which can lead to harming crop yield. To tackle this problem, precision agriculture, which leverages technology to optimize crop production while minimizing waste and environmental harm, has emerged as a viable solution. IoT-based smart irrigation management systems are an integral part of this approach and can play a vital role in achieving water efficiency goals. In this context, an open-source intelligent system that utilizes machine learning-based algorithms and monitors parameters of soil, such as its moisture and temperature, has been developed to predict the irrigation needs of a field. By forecasting the amount of water required by crops, this system can ensure that the water is utilized more efficiently. The results of the system, which has been successfully deployed on a demo scale, are very promising. The smart system has the potential to revolutionize the way irrigation is managed and help address the water efficiency challenges facing the agriculture industry.

abstract: Water scarcity is a growing concern, particularly in agriculture, where efficient water management is essential for sustainability and crop yield. This work presents an AI-based irrigation management system aimed at optimizing water utilization through the analysis of real-time soil moisture data, meteorological forecasts, and crop-specific water needs. The system employs IoT-enabled soil sensors and predictive machine learning algorithms to dynamically modify irrigation schedules, thereby substantially minimizing water waste and optimizing crop output. title: Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence in Sustainable Development Goals
source_title: Proceedings 2024 4th International Conference on Soft Computing for Security Applications Icscsa 2024
title_norm: digitalization and artificial intelligence in sustainable development goals
abstract: Digitalizing, developing digital applications and Artificial Intelligence (AI) offer a transformative means for contributing to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This study reviews the applications of AI for sustainability across different domains and it has been observed that some of the areas include energy management through smart grids and optimization algorithms, precision farming, use-cases like disease detention on crops in agriculture, water conservation-water auditing in but not limited to smart irrigation systems. Waste management, climate change mitigation through enhanced carbon cycle monitoring and the use of global artificial intelligence to improve transportation efficiency are examples. By monitoring and maintaining habitat information, AI can help endangered animals effectively: gather data on environment necessary to keep track of wild life population. It even facilitates smarter cities in sustainable urban planning with better resource utilization. While there are huge opportunities here, AI also comes with some challenges that persist around data privacy and ethics (and let's not forget the on-going concerns about the digital divide too). It underlines the value AI, one of the digitalization tools that is often seen as a driver for sustainable development yet which must be used judiciously and inclusively to promote equal benefits. Overall, AI is been used on widespread specialization with sustainability and this overview has only scratched the surface of each area; nevertheless it provides a condensed introduction to these powerful technologies for readers interested in investigating further.

title: IoT and SVM-based Smart Irrigation System for Sustainable Water Usage
source_title: Proceedings of the 2022 International Conference on Innovative Computing Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems Icses 2022
title_norm: iot and svmbased smart irrigation system for sustainable water usage
abstract: The typical farming procedure requires a significant quantity of water use, which results in water waste. An automatic watering technology is desperately required to decrease the amount of water wasted during this time-consuming activity. Because of the advancements in machine learning (ML) and the Internet of Things (IoT), there is a significant benefit to developing a smart platform that does this work successfully and with minimum human intervention. It is recommended in this paper that landowners use a minimal amount of involvement in an IoT-enabled machine learning-trained recommender system for effective water consumption. The Internet of Things (IoT) sensors are put in the agricultural field to gather accurate information about the soil and environmental condition. Upon collection, the information is moved and saved in a fog system, which uses machine learning algorithms to analysis the information and provide watering recommendations towards the producer. A built-in relay switch has been included into this suggestion system in order to make it more resilient and adaptable. The results of the experiments show that the suggested system works admirably on both our own gathered information and also the agricultural information from NIT Raipur.

title: A Low-Cost Logic-Controlled Smart Irrigation System for Sustainable Agriculture
source_title: Proceedings Icses 2026 5th International Conference on Innovative Computing Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems
title_norm: a lowcost logiccontrolled smart irrigation system for sustainable agriculture
abstract: Efficient water management is essential for sustainable agriculture, particularly in regions with limited water resources. Traditional irrigation systems often rely on manual operation, which can lead to overwatering, water wastage, and inconsistent crop growth. To overcome these challenges, this project presents a Smart Irrigation System using Arduino, designed to automate water supply and improve agricultural efficiency. The system uses a soil moisture sensor and pH sensor to continuously monitor soil conditions. Sensor readings are processed by an Arduino Uno, where simple logic gates and truth table-based decision-making determine whether irrigation is required. When soil moisture is low and no rainfall is detected, the relay module activates a 5 V water pump to deliver water to the plants. Conversely, when adequate moisture or rainfall is present, the system automatically stops irrigation to conserve water. An LED indicator is included to display water level or system status, improving reliability and ease of maintenance. Built with low- cost and readily available components, including an Arduino Uno, relay driver, and basic sensors, this system offers an efficient, scalable, and environmentally friendly irrigation solution. By combining real-time sensing with automated logic control, the Smart Irrigation System reduces human effort, prevents water wastage, and supports sustainable and intelligent farming practices.
